book_title:
The Holy Gospel of Jesus Christ
according to John.

intros.title: THE ARGUMENT OF S. JOHN'S GOSPEL.
intros.text:
S. John's Gospel may be divided into four parts.
The first part is, of the acts of Christ before his solemn manifestation of himself, while John Baptist was yet baptizing: Chap. 1. 2. 3. 4.
The second, of his Acts in Jury (having now begun his solemn manifestation in Galilee, Nat, 4, 12 (the second Easter of Pasch of his preaching: Chap. 5. For of the first Pasch, we had in the first part, chap. 2, 13: And the Pasch of the Jews was at hand. And that feast whereof we have in this [1] second part, chap. 5, 1: After this there was a festival day of the Jews, is thought of good [2] Authors, to be the feast of Pasch. Iren. li. 2. c. 39. The third part is, of this Acts in Galilee, and in Jury, about the third Pasch, and after it: cap. 6, to the 12. For so we have chap. 6, 4: and Pasch the festival day of the Jews was at hand.
The fourth part is of the fourth Pasch (which we have in the end of the chap. 11, 55: And the Pasch of the Jews was at hand ) that is to say, of the Holy Week of his Passion in Hierusalem: chap. 12.
unto the end of the book.
By which division it is manifest, that the intent of this Evangelist writing after the other three, was, to omit the Acts of Christ in Galilee, because the other three had written them at large: and to report his Acts done in Jury, which they had omitted.
And this he doth, because Iury with Hierusalem and the Temple, being the principal part of the Country, there abode the principal of the Jews, both for authority, and also for learning in the law or knowledge of the Scriptures, and therefore that was the place, where our Lord JESUS finding in the Head itself and in the leaders of the rest, such willful obstinacy and desperate resistance, as the Prophets had foretold, did by this occasion, much more plainly than in Galilee, both say and prove, at sundry times, even every year of his preaching, himself to be the CHRIST that had been so long promised unto them, & expected of them: & the same CHRIST to be not only a man, as they imagined, but also the natural, consubstantial, & coeternal Son of God the Father, who now had sent him. Therefore these were the words and deeds that served best the purpose of this Evangelist, being, to shew the glory & excellency of this person JESUS: that thereby the Gentiles might see, how worthily Hierusalem & the Jews were reprobated, who had refused yea & crucified such an one: and how well & to their own salvation themselves might do, to receive him and to believe in him. For this to have been his purpose, himself declareth in the end, saying: These are ◦ written, that you may believe that JESUS is CHRIST the Son of God: and that believing, you may have life in his name. And hereupon it is, that S. Hierome writeth thus in his life: John the Apostle, whom Jesus loved ◦ very much, the son of Zebedee, the brother of James the Apostle whom Herod after our Lord's Passion beheaded, last of all wrote the Gospel, at the request of the Bishops of Asia, against Cerinthus, and other Heretics, and specially against the assertion of the Ebionites then rising, who say that Christ was not before MARY. Whereupon also he was compelled to utter his Divine Nativity. Of his three Epistles, and of his Apocalypse, shall be said in their own places. It followeth in S. Hierome, that In the Second persecution under Domitian, for fourteen years after the persecution of Nero he was exiled into the isle Patmos. But after that Domitian was slain, and his acts for his passing cruelty repealed by the Senate: under Nerva the Emperor he returned to Ephesus, and there continuing unto the time of Trajane the Emperor, he founded and governed all the Churches of Asia: and worn with old age, he died the threescore and eight year after the Passion of our Lord, and was buried besides the same city. Whose excellency the same holy Doctor thus briefly describeth. li. 1. Advers. Iovinianum. IOHN the Apostle, one of our Lord's Disciples, who was the youngest among the Apostles, and whom the faith of Christ found a virgin, remained a virgin, and therefore is more loved of our [1] Lord, and lieth upon the breast of JESUS: and that which Peter durst not ask, he desireth him to ask: and after the resurrection, when Mary Magdalen had reported that our Lord was risen again, both of them ran to the Sepulchre, but he came thither first: and when they were in the ship [2] and fished in the lake of Genesareth, JESUS stood on the shore, neither did the Apostles know whom they saw: only the virgin knoweth the virgin, and saith to Peter, It is our Lord: This John [3] was both an Apostle, and Evangelist, and Prophet: and Apostle, because he wrote to the Churches as a Master: an Evangelist because he compiled a book of the Gospel, which (except Matthew) none other of the twelve Apostles did: a Prophet, for he saw in the isle Patmos, where he was banished by Domitian the Emperor for the testimony of our Lord, the Apocalypse, containing infinite mysteries of things to come. Tertullian also reporteth, that at Rome being cast into a barrel of hot boiling oil, he came forth more pure and fresher or livelier, than he went in. Yea and his Gospel itself much differeth from the rest. Matthew beginneth to write as of a man: Mark of the prophecy of Malachie and Esay: Luke of the Priesthood of Zachary: the first hath the face of a man, because of the genealogy: the second the face of a lion, for the voice of one crying in the desert: the third the face of a calf, because of the Priesthood. But John as an Eagle flieth to the things on high, & mounteth to the Father himself, saying: In the beginning was the WORD, and the WORD was with God, and God was the WORD. Thus far S. Hierome. Upon this Gospel there are the famous commentaries of S. Augustine called Tractatus in Evang. Ioan. to. 9. and twelve books of S. Cyril's commentaries.

verses.text: Then, the testimonies of John Baptist, first to the solemn legacy of the Jews: 29. secondly, when he saw Jesus come to him: 35. thirdly, to his own Disciples also, putting them over from himself to Jesus. Who made it plainer to them that he is Christ, 40. and so began he also to have Disciples. [1]

notes.text: The 1. parte: THE ACTES of Christ before his manifestation, whiles Iohn Baptist was yet baptizing.

verses.text: IN <na>[1]</na> THE beginning vvas the <sc>WORD</sc>, and the <sc>WORD</sc> vvas vvith God, and God vvas the <sc>WORD</sc>.

notes.text: The Gospel at the third Masse vpon Christmas day. And euery day at the end of Masse.

verses.text: This was in the beginning vvith God.
Al things vvere made by him: and vvithout him vvas made <na>[1]</na> <alt>‘nothing. That vvhich vvas made</alt>’,

notes.text: ‘nothing that was made.

verses.text: in him was life, and the life was the light of men:
and the light shineth in darkenesse, and the darkenesse did not comprehend it.
There vvas a man sent from God, vvhose name vvas Iohn.
This man came for testimonie: to giue testimonie of the light, that al might beleeue through him.
He was not the light, but to giue testimonie of the light.
It was the true light, vvhich lighteneth euery man that commeth into this vvorld.
He vvas in the vvorld, and the vvorld vvas made by him, and the vvorld knevv him not.
He came into his ovvne, and his ovvne receiued him not.
But as many as receiued him, he gaue them povver to be made the sonnes of God, to those that beleeue in his name.
VVho, not of bloud, nor of the vvil of flesh, nor of the vvil of man, but of God are borne.
<na>[1]</na> <sc>AND THE VVORD VVAS MADE FLESH</sc>, and dwelt in vs (and vve savv the glorie of him, glorie as it vvere of the only-begotten of the Father) ful of grace and veritie. ⊢

notes.text: ET VERBVM CARO FACTVM EST.

verses.text: <na>[1]</na> Iohn giueth testimonie of him, and crieth saying, This vvas he of vvhom I spake, He that shal come after me, is made before me: because he vvas before me.

notes.text: He is preferred & made of more dignitie and excellencie then I, because he was before me & al things, eternal God.

verses.text: And of his fulnes al vve haue receiued, and grace for grace.
For the lavv vvas giuen by Moyses, grace and veritie vvas made by <sc>IESVS</sc> Christ.
God no man hath seen at any time: the only begotten Sonne vvhich is in the bosome of the father, he hath declared.
<na>[1]</na> And this is Iohns testimonie, vvhen the Ievves sent from Hierusalem Priests and Leuites to him, that they should aske him, VVho art thou?

notes.text: The Gospel vpon the 3 Sunday in Aduent.

verses.text: And he confessed, and did not denie: and he confessed, That I am not <sc>CHRIST</sc>.
And they asked him, VVhat then? Art thou <cr>[1]</cr> Elias? And he said, I am not. Art thou <cr>[2]</cr><na>[3]</na> the Prophet? And he ansvvered, No.

notes.text: By like the Iewes ignorantly vnderstood not the place in Deuteronomie, of Christ, and therfore they aske also whether he be the Prophet there spoken of. See also c. 7, 40.

verses.text: They said therefore vnto him, Who art thou, that vve may giue an ansvver to them that sent vs? vvhat saiest thou of thy self?
He said, I am the voyce of one crying in the desert, make straight the vvay of our Lord, [1] as Esaie the Prophet said.
And they that vvere sent, vvere of the Pharisees.
And they asked him, and said to him, VVhy then doest thou baptize, if thou be not Christ, nor Elias, nor the Prophet?
Iohn ansvvered them, saying, <cr>[1]</cr><na>[2]</na> I baptize in vvater: but there hath stood in the middes of you vvhom you know not.

notes.text: He doth often here signifie the great difference of his baptisme & of Christs, as of his person & Christs. See Annot. Mat. 3.

verses.text: The same is he that shal come after me, that is made before me: vvhose latchet of his shoe I am not worthie to vnloose.
These things were done in Bethania beyond Iordan, vvhere Iohn vvas baptizing. ⊢
[1] The next day Iohn savv IESVS comming to him, and he saith, Behold the lambe of God, behold him that taketh avvay the [2] ‘sinne’ of the vvorld. [3]

notes.text: The Gospel on the octaue of the Epiphanie.

verses.text: This is he of vvhom I said, After me there commeth a man, vvhich is made before me: because he vvas before me.
And I knew him not, but that he may be manifested in Israel, therefore came I baptizing in vvater.
And Iohn gaue testimonie, saying, That I savv the Spirit descending as a doue from heauen, and he remained vpon him.
And I knevv him not: but he that sent me to baptize in vvater, he said to me, He vpon vvhom thou shalt see the Spirit descending and remaining vpon him, he it is that baptizeth in the holy Ghost.
And I savv: and I gaue testimonie that this is the sonne of God. ⊢
<na>[1]</na> The next day againe Iohn stoode, and tvvo of his disciples.

notes.text: The Gospel vpon S. Andrewes eue.

verses.text: And beholding <sc>IESVS</sc> vvalking, he saith, Behold the lambe of God.
And the tvvo Disciples heard him speaking, and they folovved <sc>IESVS</sc>.
And <sc>IESVS</sc> turning, and seeing them folowing him, saith to them, VVhat seeke you? VVho said to him, Rabbi (vvhich is called by interpretation, Maister) vvhere dvvellest thou?
He saith to them, Come and see. They came, and savv where he abode and they taried with him that day: and it vvas about the tenth houre.
And Andrevv the brother of Simon Peter vvas one of the tvvo that had heard of Iohn, and folovved him.
He findeth first his brother Simon, and saith to him, VVe haue found <na>[1]</na> <sc>MESSIAS</sc>, vvhich is being interpreted, <sc>CHRIST</sc>.

notes.text: Messias in Hebrue, in Greeke Christ, in English Anointed, to witte, with the spiritual oile of grace aboue his brethren. Ps. 44.

verses.text: And he brought him to IESVS. And IESVS looking vpon him, said, Thou art Simon the sonne of Iona: thou shalt be called [1] Cephas, vvhich is interpreted, Peter.

notes.text: Cephas in Syriake, & Peter in Greeke, in English Rocke. See Mat. 16, 18.

verses.text: On the morovv he vvould goe forth into Galilee, and he findeth Philippe. And <sc>IESVS</sc> saith to him, Folovv me.
And Philippe vvas of Bethsaida, the citie of Andrevv and Peter.
Philippe findeth Nathanael, and saith to him, Him whom Moyses in the lavv, and the Prophets vvrote of: vve haue found <sc>IESVS</sc> the sonne of Ioseph, of Nazareth.
And Nathanael said to him, From Nazareth can there be any good? Philippe saith to him, Come and see.
<na>[1]</na> <sc>IESVS</sc> savv Nathanael comming to him, and he saith of him, Behold an Israelite in very deede, in vvhom there is no guile.

notes.text: The Gospel in a votiue Masse of the holy Angels.

verses.text: Nathanael saith to him, Hovv knowest thou me? <sc>IESVS</sc> ansvvered and said to him, Before that Philippe did cal thee, vvhen thou wast vnder the figtree, I saw thee.
Nathanael ansvvered him, and saith, Rabbi, thou art the sonne of God, thou art the king of Israel.
<sc>IESVS</sc> ansvvered, and said to him, Because I said vnto thee, I saw thee vnder the figtree, thou beleeuest: greater then these things shalt thou see.
And he saith to him, Amen Amen I say to you, You shal see the heauen opened, and the <cr>[1]</cr> Angels of God ascending and descending, vpon the Sonne of man. ⊢

notes.text: Peter by his new

chapters.summary: The preface of the Evangelist, commending Christ (as being God the Son incarnate) to the Gentiles, and setting out the blindness of the Jews in not receiving him. 19.

verses.text: <sc>AND</sc> <na>[1]</na> the third day there vvas a mariage made in Cana of Galilee: and the mother of <sc>IESVS</sc> vvas there.

notes.text: The Gospel vpō the 2 Sunday after the Epiphanie.

verses.text: And <sc>IESVS</sc> also vvas called, and his Disciples to the mariage.
And the vvine failing, the mother of <sc>IESVS</sc> saith to him, They haue no wine.
And <sc>IESVS</sc> saith to her, VVhat is to me and thee vvoman? my houre commeth not yet.
His mother saith to the ministers, VVhatsoeuer he shal say to you, doe ye.
And there were set there sixe water-pottes of stone, according to the purification of the Ievves, holding euery one tvvo or three measures.
<sc>IESVS</sc> saith to them, Fil the vvater-pottes vvith vvater. And they filled them vp to the toppe.
And <sc>IESVS</sc> saith to them, Dravv novv, and carie to the cheefe stevvard. And they caried it.
And after the cheefe stevvard tasted the <na>[1]</na> water made vvine, and knevv not vvhence it vvas, but the ministers knew that had dravvne the vvater: the cheefe stevvard calleth the bridegrome,

notes.text: He that seeth water turned in to wine, nedeth not dispute or doubt how Christ changed bread into his body.

verses.text: and saith to him, Euery man first setteth the good vvine: and vvhen they haue vvel drunke, then that vvhich is vvorse. But thou hast kept the good vvine vntil novv.
This beginning of miracles did <sc>IESVS</sc> in Cana of Galilee: and he manifested his glorie, and his Disciples beleeued in him. ⊢
After this he vvent dovvne to Capharnaum him self and his mother, and his brethren, and his disciples: and there they remained not many daies.
<na>[1]</na> And the Pasche of the Iewes vvas at hand, and <sc>IESVS</sc> vvent vp to Hierusalem:

notes.text: The Gospel vpō Munday in the fourth weeke of Lent.

verses.text: and he found in the temple them that sold oxen and sheepe and doues, and the bankers sitting.

And vvhen he had made as it vvere a vvhippe of litle coardes, he cast them al out of the temple, the sheepe also and the oxen, and the money of the bankers he powred out, and the tables he ouerthrevv.
And to them that sold doues, he said, Take avvay these things hence, and make not the house of my father, a house of marchandise.
And his Disciples remembred that it is vvritten, The zeale of thy house hath eaten me. [1]
The Ievves therfore answered and said to him, VVhat signe doest thou shevv vs, that thou doest these things?
<sc>IESVS</sc> ansvvered and said to them, <cr>[1]</cr> Dissolue this temple, and in three daies I vvil raise it.
The Iewes therfore said, In fourtie and sixe yeres vvas this temple built, and vvilt thou raise it in three daies?
But he spake of the temple of his body.
Therfore vvhen he vvas risen againe from the dead, his Disciples remembred, that he said this, and they beleeued the scripture and the vvord that <sc>IESVS</sc> did say.
And vvhen he was at Hierusalem in the Pasche, vpon the festiual day, many beleeued in his name, seeing his signes vvhich he did.
But <sc>IESVS</sc> did not commit him self vnto them, for that he knew al,
and because it vvas not needeful for him that any should giue testimonie of man: for he knevv vvhat vvas in man. ⊢

chapters.summary: At the request of his mother he worketh his first miracle, turning water into wine at a mariage in Galilee, although the time of his manifestation be not yet come. 12 Then in Hierusalem at Pasche, being but one, and yet obscure, he throweth out of the Temple most miraculously al the marchantes. 28 And being yet of the blind Iewes asked a signe, he signifieth so long before, that they should kill him, but he wil rise againe the third day. 23 Which also presently they would doe, but that he knowing their falses hartes (though many beleeue in him) wil not tarie among them.

verses.text: <sc>AND</sc> <na>[1]</na> there vvas a man of the Pharisees, named Nicodemus, a prince of the Ievves.

notes.text: The Gospel upon Holy Rood day, or Invention of the holy Cross. Maij 3.

verses.text: This man came to <sc>IESVS</sc> by night, and said to him, Rabbi, vve knovv that thou art come from God a maister, for no man can doe these signes vvhich thou doest, vnles God be vvith him.
<sc>IESVS</sc> ansvvered, and said to him, Amen, Amen I say to thee, Vnles a man be borne againe, he can not see the kingdom of God.
Nicodemus said to him, Hovv can a man be borne, vvhen he is old? can he enter into his mothers vvombe againe and be borne?
<sc>IESVS</sc> ansvvered, Amen, Amen I say to thee, Vnles a man be borne againe of vvater and the Spirit, he can not enter into the kingdom of God.
That vvhich is borne of the flesh, is flesh: & that vvhich is borne of the spirit, is spirit.
Marueil not, that I said to thee, You must be borne againe.
The spirit breatheth vvhere <na>[1]</na> he vvil: and thou hearest his voice, but thou knovvest not vvhence he commeth and vvhither he goeth: so is euery one that is borne of the Spirit.

notes.text: We folow rather S. August. & those ancient fathers, which most commōly vnderstand this place of the holy Ghost, & not of the winde: although both senses be good.

verses.text: Nicodemus ansvvered, & said to him, Hovv can these things be done?
<sc>IESVS</sc> ansvvered, and said to him, Thou art a maister in Israel, and art thou ignorant of these things?
Amen, Amen I say to thee, that we speake that vvhich vve knovv, and that vvhich vve haue seen vve testifie, and our testimonie you receiue not.
If I haue spoken to you earthly things, and you beleeue not: how if I shal speake to you heauenly things, vvil you beleeue?
And no man hath ascended into heauen, but he that descended from heauen, the Sonne of man vvhich is in heauen.
And as <cr>[1]</cr> Moyses exalted the serpent in the desert, so must the Sonne of man be exalted:
that euery one vvhich beleeueth in him, perish not, but may haue life euerlasting.
<na>[1]</na> For so God loued the vvorld, that he gaue his only-begotten sonne: that euery one that beleeueth in him, perish not, but may haue life euerlasting. ⊢

notes.text: The Gospel vpō Munday in the whitsonweeke.

verses.text: For God sent not his sonne into the vvorld, to iudge the vvorld, but that the vvorld may be saued by him.
He that beleeueth in him, is not iudged. but he that doeth not beleeue, is already iudged: because he hath not beleeued in the name of the only-begotten sonne of God.
And this is the iudgment: because the light is come into the vvorld, and men haue loued the darkenesse rather then the light: for their vvorkes vvere euil.
For euery one that doeth il, hateth the light, and commeth not to the light, that his vvorkes may not be controuled.
But he that doeth veritie, commeth to the light, that his vvorkes may be made manifest, because they vvere done in God. ⊢
After these things <sc>IESVS</sc> came and his Disciples into the countrie of Ievvrie: and there he abode vvith them, and baptized.
And Iohn also vvas baptizing in Aenon beside Salim: because there vvas much vvater there, and they came, and vvere baptized.
For Iohn vvas not yet cast into prison.
And there rose a question of Iohns disciples vvith the Ievves concerning purification.
And they came to Iohn, and said to him, Rabbi, he that vvas vvith thee beyond Iordan, to whom <cr>[1]</cr> thou didst giue testimonie, behold he baptizeth, and al come to him.
Iohn ansvvered and said, A man can not receiue any thing, vnlesse it be giuen him from heauen.
Your selues doe beare me vvitnesse, <cr>[1]</cr> that I said, I am not <sc>CHRIST</sc>: but that I am sent before him.
He that hath the bride, is the bridegrome: but the frende of the bridegrome that standeth and heareth him, reioyceth vvith ioy for the voice of the bridegrome. This my ioy therfore is filled.
He must increase, and I diminishe.
He that commeth from aboue, is aboue al. He that is of the earth, of the earth he is, and of the earth he speaketh. He that commeth from heauen, is aboue al.
And vvhat he hath seen and heard, that he testifieth: and his testimonie no man receiueth.
He that hath receiued his testimonie, hath signed that God is true.
For he vvhom God hath sent, speaketh the vvordes of God. for God doth not giue the spirit by measure.
The Father loueth the Sonne: & he hath giuen al things in his hand.
He that beleeueth in the Sonne, hath life euerlasting: but he that is incredulous to the Sonne, shal not see life, but the vvrath of God remaineth vpon him.

chapters.summary: He teacheth Nicodemus, that to come to the kingdom of God, Baptisme is necessarie, as being our Regeneration. 10 Which point Nicodemus as then not vnderstāding, 11 he sheweth that they must beleeue him, and what good cause there is for them so to doe. 23. After this he also baptizeth, and Iohn likewise at the same time. 25 Wherevpon a question being moued, Whether Baptisme is better, 25 Iohn answereth it by saying, that he is so far inferiour to Christ, as a mere man to God most high.

verses.text: <sc>WHEN IESVS</sc> therfore vnderstoode that the Pharisees heard that <sc>IESVS</sc> maketh mo Disciples, and baptizeth, then Iohn,
(hovvbeit <na>[1]</na> <sc>IESVS</sc> did not baptize, but his Disciples)

notes.text: He did not baptize ordinarily. yet that he baptized his Apostles, S. Aug. thinketh it very probable, ep. 108.

verses.text: he left Iewrie, and vvent againe into Galilee.
and he had of necessitie to passe through Samaria.
<cr>[1]</cr> He commeth therfore into a citie of Samaria vvhich is called Sichar: <na>[2]</na> beside the maner that Iacob gaue to Ioseph his sonne.

notes.text: The Gospel vpō Friday in the 3 weeke in Lent.

verses.text: And there vvas there the fountaine of Iacob. <sc>IESVS</sc> therfore vvearied of his iourney, sate so vpon the fountaine. It vvas about the sixt houre.
There commeth <na>[1]</na> a vvoman of Samaria to dravv water, <sc>IESVS</sc> saith to her, Giue me to drinke.

notes.text: This woman is a figure of the Church, not yet iustified, but now to be iustified. Aug. tract. 15 in Ioan.

verses.text: For his Disciples vvere gone into the citie, to bie meates.
Therfore that Samaritane vvoman saith to him, How doest thou being a Ievve, aske of me to drinke, vvhich am a Samaritane woman? For the Iewes <na>[1]</na> do not communicate vvith the Samaritanes.

notes.text: There were many other causes why the faithful Iewes could not abide the Samaritans, but their precise abstaining from their companie & cōuersation, was their Schismatical Temple and seruice in moūt Garîzim.

verses.text: <sc>IESVS</sc> ansvvered, and said to her, If thou didst know the gift of God, and vvho he is that saith vnto thee, Giue me to drinke: thou perhaps vvouldest haue asked of him, and he would haue giuen thee c liuing vvater.
The woman saith to him, Sir, neither hast thou vvherein to dravv, and the vvel is deepe: whence hast thou the liuing water?
art thou greater then our father Iacob, who gaue vs the wel, and him self dranke of it, and his children, and his cattel?
<sc>IESVS</sc> answered, and said to her, Euery one that drinketh of this water, shal thirst againe: <na>[1]</na> but he that shal drinke of the water that I wil giue him, shal not thirst for euer,

notes.text: He speaketh of his baptizing in the Holy Ghost. See Io. c. 7, 39.

verses.text: but the vvater that I vvil giue him, shal become in him a fountaine of water springing vp vnto life euerlasting.
The vvoman saith to him, Lord giue me this vvater, that I may not thirst, nor come hither to dravv.
<sc>IESVS</sc> saith to her, Goe, call thy husband, and come hither.
The vvoman ansvvered and said, I haue no husband. <sc>IESVS</sc> saith to her, Thou hast said vvel, that I haue no husband.
For thou hast had fiue husbands: and he vvhom thou novv hast, is not thy husband. this thou hast said truely.
The woman saith to him, Lord, I perceiue that thou art a Prophet.
Our fathers adored in this mountaine, and you say, <cr>[1]</cr> that at Hierusalem is the place vvhere men must adore.
<sc>IESVS</sc> saith to her, VVoman beleeue me, that the houre shal come, vvhen you shal neither in this mountaine, nor in Hierusalem adore the Father.
<cr>[1]</cr> You adore that you knovv not: vve adore that vve knovv, for saluation is of the Ievves.
But the houre commeth, and novv it is, vvhen the true adorers shal adore the Father in spirit and veritie. for the Father also seeketh such, to adore him.
God is a spirit, and they that adore him, must adore in spirit and veritie.
The vvoman saith to him, I know that <sc>MESSIAS</sc> commeth, (vvhich is called <sc>CHRIST</sc>): therfore when he commeth, he vvil shevv vs al things.
<sc>IESVS</sc> saith to her, I am he, that speake with thee.
And incontinent his Disciples came: and they marueiled that he talked vvith a vvoman. No man for al that said, VVhat seekest thou, or why talkest thou with her?
The woman therfore left her vvater-pot: and she vvent into the citie, and saith to those men,
Come, and see a man that hath told me al things vvhatsoeuer I haue done. Is not he <sc>CHRIST</sc>?
They vvent forth therfore out of the citie, and came to him.
In the meane time the Disciples desired him, saying, Rabbi eate.
But he said to them, I haue meate to eate which you knovv not.
The Disciples therfore said one to an other, Hath any man brought him for to eate?
<sc>IESVS</sc> saith to them, My meate is to doe the vvil of him that sent me, to perfit his vvorke.
Doe not you say that yet there are foure moneths, and haruest commeth? Behold I say to you, lift vp your eies, and see the countries, that they are vvhite already to haruest.
And he that reapeth, receiueth hire, and gathereth fruite vnto life euerlasting: that both he that sovveth, and he that reapeth, may reioyce together.
For in this is the saying true: that it is one man that sovveth, and it is an other that reapeth.
I haue sent you to reape that vvhich you laboured not: others haue laboured, and you haue entred into their labours.
And of that citie many beleeued in him of the Samaritans, for the vvord of the <na>[1]</na> vvoman giuing testimonie, that he told me al things vvhatsoeuer I haue done.

notes.text: This woman mystically being the Church, it is here signified, that they which at the first beleeue because the Church teacheth so, afterward be much confirmed, finding it in the Scripture also, and by other instructions.

verses.text: Therfore vvhen the Samaritans vvere come to him, they desired him that he vvould tarie there. And he taried there tvvo daies.
And many moe beleeued for his ovvne vvord.
And they said to the vvoman, That novv not for thy saying doe vve beleeue: for our selues haue heard, and doe knovv that this is the Sauiour of the vvorld in deede. ⊢
And after the tvvo daies he departed thence: and vvent into Galilee.
For <sc>IESVS</sc> him self gaue testimonie that a Prophet hath not honour in his ovvne countrie.

Therfore <cr>[1]</cr> vvhen he vvas come into Galilee, the Galilaeans receiued him, vvhereas they had seen al things that he had done at Hierusalem in the festiual day: for them selues also came to the festiual day.
<cr>[1]</cr> He came againe therfore into Cana of Galilee, <na>[2]</na> VVhere he made vvater vvine. And there vvas a certaine lord vvhose sonne was sicke at Capharnáum.

notes.text: The Gospel vpō the 20 Sunday after Pentecost.

verses.text: He hauing heard that <sc>IESVS</sc> came from Ievvrie into Galilee, vvent to him, and desired him that he vvould come dovvne & heale his sonne. for he began to die.
<sc>IESVS</sc> therfore said to him, Vnlesse you see signes and vvonders, you beleeue not.
The lord saith to him, Lord, come dovvne before that my sonne die.
<sc>IESVS</sc> saith to him, Goe, thy sonne liueth. The man beleeued the vvord that <sc>IESVS</sc> said to him, and went.
And as he was novv going downe, his seruants mette him: and they brought vvord, saying, That his sonne liued.
He asked therfore of them the houre, vvherein he vvas amended. And they said to him, That yesterday at the seuenth houre the feuer left him.
The father therfore knew that it was in the same houre vvherein <sc>IESVS</sc> said to him, Thy sonne liueth. and him self beleeued and his vvhole house. ⊢
This againe the <cr>[1]</cr> second signe did <sc>IESVS</sc>, vvhen he vvas come from Ievvrie into Galilee.

chapters.summary: Leauing Iewrie because of the Pharisees, in the way to Galilee he talketh with a Samaritane woman, telling her that he wil giue water of euerlasting life, 16 shewing him self to know mens secretes, 19 preferring the Iewes religion before the Samaritanes, but ours (the Christian Catholike religion) before them both, 25 and vttering vnto her that he is Christ. 28 which by her testimonie and his preaching very many Samaritanes do beleeue: he in the meane time fore telling his Disciples, of the haruest he wil send them in to. 45 The Galilaeans also receiue him, where againe he worketh his second miracle.

verses.text: <sc>AFTER</sc> <na>[1]</na> these things there vvas a festiual day of the Ievves, and <sc>IESVS</sc> went vp to Hierusalem.

notes.text: The Gospel vpō friday in the first weeke of Lent.

verses.text: And there is at Hierusalem <alt>‘vpon</alt>’ <na>[1]</na> Probatica a pond which in hebrevv is surnamed <na>[2]</na> <alt>‘Bethsaida</alt>’, hauing fiue porches.

notes.text: By our latin text and the Greeke, this miraculous pond was in or vpon Probatica, that is, a place where the sheepe to be sacrificed, were kept. But by other latin copies, S. Hierom, and some Greeke fathers, Probatica is the very pōd it self: so called, because the sheepe of sacrifice were there washed.
Bethesda,

verses.text: In these lay a great multitude of sicke persons, of blinde, lame, vvithered, expecting the stirring of the vvater.

And an Angel of our Lord descended at a certaine time into the pond: and the water vvas stirred. And he that had gone dovvne first into the pond after the stirring of the water, was made vvhole of vvhatsoeuer infirmitie he vvas holden.
And there vvas a certaine man there that had been eight and thirtie yeres in his infirmitie.
Him when <sc>IESVS</sc> had seen lying, & knevv that c <na>[1]</na> he had now a long time, he saith to him, Wilt thou be made vvhole?

notes.text: multū tempus haberet,

verses.text: The sicke man answered him, Lord, I haue no man, when the vvater is troubled, to put me into the pond. For whiles I come, an other goeth dovvne before me.
<sc>IESVS</sc> saith to him, Arise, take vp thy bed, and vvalke.
And forthvvith he vvas made whole: and he tooke vp his bed, and vvalked. And it vvas the Sabboth that day.
The Ievves therfore said to him that vvas healed, It is the Sabboth, thou maist not take vp thy bed.
He answered them, He that made me vvhole, he said to me, Take vp thy bed, and walke.
They asked him therfore, VVhat is that man that said to thee, Take vp thy bed, and vvalke?
But he that vvas made vvhole, knevv not who it was. For <sc>IESVS</sc> shronke aside from the multitude standing in the place.
Aftervvard <sc>IESVS</sc> findeth him in the temple, and said to him, Behold thou art made vvhole: sinne no more, lest some vvorse thing chaunce to thee.
That man went his way, and told the Ievves that it was <sc>IESVS</sc> that made him whole. ⊢
Therevpon the Iewes persecuted <sc>IESVS</sc>, because he did these things on the Sabboth.
But <sc>IESVS</sc> answered them, My father worketh vntil novv: and I doe vvorke.
Therevpon therefore the Iewes sought the more to kil him: because he did not only breake the Sabboth, but also he said God was his father, making him self aequal to God.

<sc>IESVS</sc> therfore ansvvered, and said to them, Amen, amen I say to you, The Sonne can not doe any thing of him self, but that vvhich he seeth the Father doing. For what things soeuer he doeth, these the Sonne also doeth in like maner.
For the Father loueth the Sonne, and sheweth him al things that him self doeth, and greater workes then these wil he shew him, that you may marueil.
For as the Father doth raise the dead and quickeneth: so the Sonne also quickeneth whom he wil.
For neither doth the Father iudge any man: but al iudgement he hath giuen to the Sonne,
that al may honour the Sonne, as they doe honour the Father. He that honoureth not the Sonne, doth not honour the Father, who sent him.

Amen, amen I say to you, that he which heareth my word, and beleeueth him that sent me, hath life euerlasting. and he commeth not into iudgement, but <na>[1]</na> <alt>‘shal passe</alt>’ from death into life.

notes.text: is passed.

verses.text: <na>[1]</na> Amen, amen I say to you, that the houre commeth, and now it is, when the dead shal heare the voice of the Sonne of God, and they that haue heard, shal liue.

notes.text: The Gospel upon All souls day.

verses.text: For as the Father hath life in him self: so he hath giuen to the Sonne also to haue life in him self:
and he hath giuen him power to doe iudgement also, because he is the Sonne of man.
Marueil not at this, because the houre commeth wherein al that are in the graues, shal heare his voice,
and they that haue <na>[1]</na> done good things, shal come forth into the resurrection of life: but they that haue done euil, into the resurrection of iudgement. ⊢

notes.text: Not faith only, but good and il deedes shal be counted, and accordingly rewarded at the day of iudgement.

verses.text: I can not of my self doe any thing. As I heare, so I iudge: and my iudgement is iust. because I seeke not my wil, but the wil of him that sent me.
If I giue testimonie of my self, my testimonie is not true.
There is an other that giueth testimonie of me: and I know that the testimonie is true which he giueth of me.
<cr>[1]</cr> You sent to Iohn: and he gaue testimonie to the truth.
But I receiue not testimonie of man: but I say these things that you may be saued.
He was the lampe burning and shining. And you would for a time reioyce in his light.
But I haue a greater testimonie then Iohn. For the workes which the Father hath giuen me to perfit them: the very workes them selues which I doe, giue testimonie of me, that the Father hath sent me.
And the Father that sent me, him self hath <cr>[1]</cr> giuen testimonie of me. neither haue you heard his voice at any time, nor seen his shape,
and his word you haue not remaining in you: because whom he hath sent, him you beleeue not.
Search the <na>[1]</na> scriptures, for you thinke in them to haue life euerlasting: and the same are they that giue testimonie of me:

notes.text: Catholikes searche the scriptures, and finde there, Peters & his successors Primacie, the real presence, the Priests power to forgiue sinnes, iustification by faith & good workes, Virginitie preferred before matrimonie, breach of the vow of cōtinencie damnable, voluntarie pouertie, Penāce, almes, and good deedes meritorious, diuers rewardes ĩ heauē accordĩg to diuers merites, & such like.

verses.text: and you vvil not come to me that you may haue life.
Glorie of men I receiue not.
But I haue knovven you, that the loue of God you haue not in you.
I am come in the name of my Father, and you receiue me not: if <na>[1]</na> an other shal come in his ovvne name, him you vvil receiue.

notes.text: He meaneth specially Antichrist. How then can the

verses.text: Hovv can you beleeue, that receiue glorie one of an other: and the glorie vvhich is of God only, you seeke not?
Thinke not that I vvil accuse you to the Father. there is that accuseth you, Moyses, in whom you trust.
For if you did beleeue Moyses: you vvould perhaps beleeue me also. for of me he hath written.
And if you doe not beleeue his vvritings: hovv vvil you beleeue my vvordes?

chapters.summary: Curing a bedred man at the pond of miracle, because he doth it on the Sabboth, the blind Iewes do persecute him, 7 and againe because he saith that God is his natural father. 19 He therevpon continueth saying, the Fathers operation and his to be in euery thing al one, and that he shal do greater things then these miraculous cures, to wit, 21 quicken the dead in soule by sinne, as being appointed Iudge of al, 28 yea and quicken the dead in bodies also. incontinent iudging al vprightly. 31 And that these are not bragges of his owne, but his witnesses to be, 33 Iohn Baptist, 36 his owne miraculous workes, 37 his fathers voice at his baptisme, 39 the Scriptures also, namely of Moyses. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text: The 2. part: THE ACTS of Christ in Jewry (having already begun his solemn Manifestation in Galilee Mt. 4, 12) the second Pasch of his preaching.

verses.text: <sc>AFTER</sc> <cr>[1]</cr><na>[2]</na> these things <sc>IESVS</sc> went beyond the sea of Galilee, vvhich is of Tiberias:

notes.text: The Gospel vpon Midlent Sunday.

verses.text: and a great multitude folovved him, because they savv the signes vvhich he did vpon those that vvere sicke.
<sc>IESVS</sc> therfore went vp into the mountaine, and there he sate vvith his Disciples.
And the Pasche vvas at hand, the festiual day of the Iewes.
When <sc>IESVS</sc> therfore had lifted vp his eies, and savv that a very great multitude commeth to him, he saith to Philippe, VVhence shal vve bie bread: that these may eate?
And this he said, tempting him. for him self knevv vvhat he vvould doe?
Philippe ansvvered him, Tvvo hundred penie vvorth of bread is not sufficient for them, that euery man may take a litle peece.
One of his Disciples, Andrevv the brother of Simon Peter, saith to him,
There is a boy here that hath fiue barley loaues, & tvvo fishes: but vvhat are these among so many?
<sc>IESVS</sc> therfore saith, Make the men to sit dovvne. And there vvas much grasse in the place. The men therfore sate dovvne, in number about fiue thousand.
<sc>IESVS</sc> therfore tooke the loaues: and vvhen he had giuen thankes, he distributed to them that sate. in like maner also of the fishes as much as they vvould.
And after they vvere filled, he said to his Disciples, Gather the fragments that are remaining, lest they be lost.
They gathered therfore, and filled tvvelue baskets vvith fragments of the fiue barley loaues, vvhich remained to them that had eaten.
Those men therfore vvhen they had seen vvhat a signe <sc>IESVS</sc> had done, said, That this is the Prophet in deede that is to come into the vvorld.
<sc>IESVS</sc> therfore when he knevv that they vvould come to take him, and make him king, <cr>[1]</cr> he fled againe into the mountaine him self alone. ⊢
And vvhen euen vvas come, his Disciples vvent dovvne to the sea.
And vvhen they vvere gone vp into the shippe, they came beyond the sea into Capharnáum. and now it vvas darke, and <sc>IESVS</sc> vvas not come vnto them
And the sea arose, by reason of a great vvinde that blevv.
VVhen they had rovved therfore about fiue and tvventie or thirtie furlonges, they see <sc>IESVS</sc> vvalking vpon the sea, and to dravv nigh to the shippe, and they feared.
But he saith to them, It is I, feare not.
They vvould therfore haue taken him into the shippe: and forthvvith the shippe vvas at the land to vvhich they went.

The next day, the multitude that stoode beyond the sea, savv that there vvas no other boate there but one, and that <sc>IESVS</sc> had not entred into the boate vvith his Disciples, but that his Disciples only vvere departed:
but other boates came in from Tiberias beside the place vvhere they had eaten the bread, our Lord <na>[1]</na> giuing thankes.

notes.text: These wordes do plainly import, that the giuing thankes was an effectual blessing of the bread and working the multiplication thereof.

verses.text: VVhen therfore the multitude savv that <sc>IESVS</sc> vvas not there, nor his Disciples, they vvent vp into the boates, & came to Capharnaum seeking <sc>IESVS</sc>.
And when they had found him beyond the sea, they said to him, Rabbi, when camest thou hither?
<sc>IESVS</sc> answered them, and said, Amen, amen I say to you, you seeke me not because you haue seene signes, but because you did eate of the loaues, and vvere filled.
VVorke not the meate that perisheth, but that endureth vnto life euerlasting, vvhich the Sonne of man vvil giue you. For him the Father, God, hath signed.
They said therfore vnto him, VVhat shal vve doe that vve may vvorke the vvorkes of God?
<sc>IESVS</sc> ansvvered, and said to them, This is the vvorke of God, that you beleeue in him vvhom he hath sent.
They said therfore to him, VVhat signe therfore doest thou, that vve may see, and may beleeue thee? vvhat vvorkest thou?
Our [1] fathers did eate Manna in the desert, as it is written, Bread from heauen he gaue them to eate.
<sc>IESVS</sc> therfore said to them, <na>[1]</na> Amen, amen I say to you, Moyses gaue you not the bread from heauen, but my Father giueth you the true bread from heauen.

notes.text: why we keepe the hebrue word, Amen, & translate it not, See the Annot. c. 8. vers. 34.

verses.text: For the bread of God it is that descendeth from heauen, and giueth life to the vvorld.
They said therfore vnto him, Lord, giue vs alvvaies this bread.
And <sc>IESVS</sc> said to them, I am the bread of life, he that commeth to me, shal not hunger: and he that beleeueth in me, shal neuer thirst.
But I said to you that both you haue seen me and you beleeue not.
<na>[1]</na> Al that the Father giueth me, shal come to me: and him that commeth to me I vvil not cast forth.

notes.text: The Gospel in the Anniuersarie of the dead.

verses.text: Because I descended from heauen, not to doe mine ovvne vvil, but the vvil of him that sent me.
For this is the vvil of him that sent me, the Father: that al that he hath giuen me I leese not thereof, but raise it in the last day.
And this is the vvil of my father that sent me: that euery one that seeth the Sonne, and beleeueth in him, haue life euerlasting, and I vvil raise him in the last day. ⊢
The Ievves therfore murmured at him, because he had said, I am the bread vvhich descended from heauen:
and they said, Is not this <sc>IESVS</sc> the sonne of Ioseph, vvhose father and mother vve knovv? Hovv then saith he, That I descended from heauen?
<sc>IESVS</sc> therfore ansvvered and said to them, Murmure not one to an other:
<na>[1]</na> no man can come to me, vnles the Father that sent me, dravv him: and I vvil raise him vp in the last day.

notes.text: The Gospel upon Imber Wednesday in Whitsunweek.

verses.text: It is vvritten in the Prophets, And al shal be docible of God. [1] Euery one that hath heard of the Father, and hath learned, commeth to me.
Not that any man hath seen the Father, but he vvhich is of God: this hath seen the Father.
Amen, amen I say to you, he that beleeueth in me, hath life euerlasting.
I am the bread of life.
Your fathers did eate Manna in the desert: and they died.
This is the bread that descendeth from heauen: that if any man eate of it, he die not.

<na>[1]</na> I am the liuing bread, that came dovvne from heauen. If any man eate of this bread, he shal liue for euer: and <cr>[1]</cr> the bread vvhich I vvil giue, is my flesh for the life of the vvorld. ⊢

notes.text: The Gospel in a daily Masse for the dead.

verses.text: The Ievves therfore stroue among them selues, saying, How can this man giue vs his flesh to eate?
<sc>IESVS</sc> therfore said to them, Amen, amen I say to you, Vnles you eate the flesh of the Sonne of man, and drinke his bloud, you shal not haue life in you.
He that eateth my flesh, and drinketh my bloud, hath life euerlasting: and I vvil raise him vp in the last day. ⊢
<na>[1]</na> For my flesh, is meate in deede: and my bloud is drinke in deede.

notes.text: The Gospel vpon CORPVS CHRISTI day.

verses.text: He that eateth my flesh, and drinketh my bloud, abideth in me, and I in him.
As the liuing father hath sent me, and I liue by the father: and he that eateth me, the same also shal liue by me.
This is the bread that came dovvne from heauen. Not as your fathers did eate Manna, and died. He that eateth this bread, shal liue for euer. ⊢
These things he said teaching in the Synagogue, in Capharnáum.
Many therfore of his Disciples hearing it, said, This saying is hard, and vvho can heare it?
But <sc>IESVS</sc> knovving vvith him self that his Disciples murmured at this, he said to them, Doth this scandalize you?
If then you shal see <cr>[1]</cr> the Sonne of man ascend vvhere he vvas before?
It is the spirit that quickeneth, the flesh profiteth nothing. The wordes that I haue spoken to you, be spirit and life.
But there be certaine of you that beleeue not. For <sc>IESVS</sc> knevv from the beginning vvho they vvere that did not beleeue, and vvho he vvas that vvould betray him.
And he said, Therfore did I say to you, that no man can come to me, vnles it be giuen him of my Father.
After this many of his Disciples vvent backe: and novv they vvalked not vvith him.
<sc>IESVS</sc> therfore said to the Tvvelue, VVhat, vvil you also depart?
Simon Peter therfore answered him, Lord, to vvhom shal vve goe? thou hast the vvordes of eternal life.
And we beleeue and haue knovven that thou art Christ the sonne of God.
<sc>IESVS</sc> answered them, Haue not I chosen you the Tvvelue: & of you one is a deuil?
And he meant Iudas Iscariot, Simons sonne: for this same vvas to betray him, vvhereas he was one of the Twelue.

chapters.summary: Hauing with fiue loaues fed fiue thousand 16 (walking also the night after vpon the sea) 22 on the morow the people there vpon resorting vnto him, 27 he preacheth vnto them of the Bread which he wil giue: telling them that he is come from heauen, and therfore able to giue such bread as can quicken the world, euen his owne flesh: and that al his Elect shal beleeue as much. 60 Many notwithstanding do murmur at this doctrine, yea and become apostataes, thoug he tel them that they shal see by his Ascension into heauen, that he is descended from heauen. but the Twelue sticke vnto him, beleeuing that he is God omnipotent, as he said. Among whom also (that no man be scandalized) he signifieth that he foreknoweth which wil become a traitor: as among the foresaid, which would become apostataes. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text: The 3. part. His ACTS in Galilee, & in Jewry, about the third Pasch and after.

verses.text: <sc>AFTER</sc> <na>[1]</na> these things <sc>IESVS</sc> vvalked <na>[2]</na> <alt>‘into Galilee</alt>’, for he vvould not vvalke <na>[3]</na> <alt>‘into Iewrie</alt>’: because the Iewes sought to kil him.

notes.text: The Gospel vpon Tuesday in Passion weeke.

verses.text: And the festiual day of the Ievves, <cr>[1]</cr> <na>[2]</na> Scenopégia, was at hand.

notes.text: Scenopégia (Leu.23 σκηνῶν ἑορτὴ) is the feast of Tabernacles, which the Iewes kept from the 7 octob. for eight daies together, by Gods commaundement, for a memorie that their fathers dwelt by Gods protection fourtie yeres in tabernacles or tentes, and not in houses, comming out of AEgypt. See Leuit. 23, 34.

verses.text: And his brethren said to him, Passe from hence, and goe into Ievvrie: that thy Disciples also may see thy vvorkes vvhich thou doest.
For no man doeth any thing in secrete, and seeketh him self to be in publike. If thou doe these things, manifest thy self to the vvorld.
For neither did his brethren beleeue in him.
<sc>IESVS</sc> therfore saith to them, My time is not yet come: but your time is alvvaies readie.
The vvorld can not hate you. but me it hateth: because I giue testimonie of it, that the vvorkes there of are euil.
Goe you vp to this festiual day: <na>[1]</na> <alt>‘I goe not vp</alt>’ to this festiual day: because my time is not yet accomplished.

notes.text: I will not yet go up

xrefs: I wil not yet goe vp

verses.text: When he had said these things, him self taried in Galilee.
But after his brethren vvere gone vp, then he also went vp to the festiual day, not openly, but as it vvere in secrete.
The Ievves therfore sought him in the festiual day, and said, VVhere is he?
And there vvas much murmuring in the multitude of him. For certaine said, That he is good. And others said, No, but he seduceth the multitudes.
Yet no man spake openly of him for feare of the Iewes. ⊢
<na>[1]</na> And when the festiuitie vvas novv halfe done, <sc>IESVS</sc> vvent vp into the temple, and taught.

notes.text: The Gospel vpon Tuesday in the 4 weeke of Lent.

verses.text: And the Iewes marueiled, saying, Hovv doth this man know letters, vvhereas he hath not learned?
<sc>IESVS</sc> answered them, and said, My doctrine is not mine, but his that sent me.
If any man <na>[1]</na> vvil doe the vvil of him, he shal vnderstand of the doctrine vvhether it be of God, or I speake of my self.

notes.text: The way to come to know the truth, is to liue wel.

verses.text: <na>[1]</na> He that speaketh of him self, seeketh his ovvne glorie. But he that seeketh the glorie of him that sent him, he is true, and iniustice in him there is not.

notes.text: It is spoken of Antichrist specially, and it is true in al Heretikes. August. tract. 29. in Euang. Io.

verses.text: Did not Moyses giue you the lavv, and none of you doeth the lavv?
<cr>[1]</cr> VVhy seeke you to kil me? The multitude ansvvered, and said, <na>[2]</na> Thou hast a deuil, who seeketh to kil thee?

notes.text: No maruel, when these speake thus to Christ him self, if Heretikes call his vicar Antichrist.

verses.text: <sc>IESVS</sc> ansvvered, and said to them, One vvorke I haue done: and you doe al marueil.
Therfore <cr>[1]</cr> Moyses gaue you circuncision: not that it is of Moyses, but <cr>[2]</cr> of the fathers, and in the Sabboth you circuncise a man.
If a man receiue circuncision in the Sabboth, that the lavv of Moyses be not broken: are you angrie at me because I haue healed a man vvholy in the Sabboth?
Iudge not according to the face, but iudge iust iudgement.
Certaine therfore of Hierusalem said, Is not this he vvhom they seeke to kil?
And behold, he speaketh openly, and they say nothing to him. Haue the Princes knovven in deede that this is <sc>CHRIST</sc>?
But this man vve knovv whence he is. But vvhen <sc>CHRIST</sc> commeth, no man knovveth vvhence he is.
<sc>IESVS</sc> therfore cried in the temple teaching, and saying, Both me you doe knovv, and vvhence I am you knovv. And of my self I am not come, but he is true that sent me, vvhom you knovv not.
I knovv him, because I am of him, and he sent me.
They sought therfore to apprehend him: and no man laide handes vpon him, because his houre vvas not yet come.
But of the multitude many beleeued in him, ⊢ and said, <sc>CHRIST</sc> vvhen he commeth, shal he doe more signes then these vvhich this man doeth?
The Pharisees heard the multitude murmuring these things touching him: and the <na>[1]</na> <alt>‘Princes</alt>’ and Pharisees sent ministers to apprehend him.

notes.text: chief Priests

verses.text: <na>[1]</na> <sc>IESVS</sc> therfore said to them, Yet a litle time I am vvith you: and I goe to him that sent me.

notes.text: The Gospel vpon Munday in Passion weeke.

verses.text: <cr>[1]</cr> You seeke me, and shal not finde: and vvhere I am, you can not come.
The Ievves therfore said among them selues, VVhither vvil this man goe, that vve shal not finde him? VVil he goe into the dispersion of the Gentiles, and teach the Gentiles?
VVhat is this saying that he hath said, You shal seeke me, and shal not finde: And vvhere I am, you can not come.
And in the last, the <cr>[1]</cr> great day of the festiuitie <sc>IESVS</sc> stoode, and cried, saying, If any man thirst, let him come to me, and drinke.
He that beleeueth in me, as the scripture saith, Out of his belly shal flovv riuers of liuing vvater. [1]
(And this he said <cr>[1]</cr> of the Spirit that they should receiue vvhich beleeued in him. ⊢ <na>[2]</na> for as yet the Spirit vvas not giuen: because <sc>IESVS</sc> vvas not yet glorified.)

notes.text: This was fulfilled on whitsunday Act. 2, & afterward alwaies by imposition of hands in the Sacrament of Confirmation: visibly in the primitiue Church, and inuisibly to the end of the world.

verses.text: Of that multitude therfore, vvhen they had heard these wordes of his, some said, This is the Prophet in deede.
others said, This is <sc>CHRIST</sc>. But certaine said, VVhy, doth <sc>CHRIST</sc> come from Galilee?
Doth not the <cr>[1]</cr> scripture say, that of the seede of Dauid, and from Bethlehem the tovvne vvhere Dauid vvas, <sc>CHRIST</sc> doth come?
Therfore there arose dissension in the multitude for him.
And certaine of them vvould haue apprehended him: but no man laid handes vpon him.
The ministers therfore came to the cheefe priests and the Pharisees. And they said to them, VVhy haue you not brought him?
The ministers ansvvered, Neuer did there man so speake, as this man.
The Pharisees therfore ansvvered them, VVhy, are you also seduced?
Hath any of the Princes beleeued in him, or of the Pharisees?
but this multitude that knovveth not the lavv, are accursed.
Nicodemus said to them, <cr>[1]</cr> he <na>[2]</na> that came to him by night, who vvas one of them,

notes.text: Christ hath some good alwaies euen among the wicked, which secretly serue him and by wise delaies auert the execution of vniust lawes against him and his people, as Nicodemꝰ and Gamaliel.

verses.text: Doth our lavv iudge a man, vnles it first heare him, and knovv vvhat he doeth?
They ansvvered, and said to him, VVhy, art thou also a Galilaean? Search, <na>[1]</na> and see that from Galilee a Prophet riseth not.

notes.text: Search the scriptures

verses.text: And euery man returned to his house.

chapters.summary: The Iewes (of Hierusalem) seeking his death, he walketh in Galilee: where he signifieth to his brethren, that not in this feast Scenopégia, but in an other (to wit, Pasche folowing) the Iewes should kil him: that is, not when they would, but when he wil. 10 In so much that at this feast he teacheth openly in the Temple, and conuerteth many, 14 both in the middle day 37 and the last day thereof, without any hurt, though also the Rulers send to apprehend him.

verses.text: <sc>AND <na>[1]</na> IESVS</sc> vvent into the Mount-oliuet:

notes.text: The Gospel vpon Saturday the 3 Weeke of Lent.

verses.text: and early in the morning againe he came into the temple, and the people came to him, and sitting he taught them.
And the Scribes and Pharisees bring a vvoman taken in aduoutrie: and they did set her in the middes,
and said to him, Maister, this woman vvas euen novv taken in aduoutrie.
And <cr>[1]</cr> in the lavv Moyses commaunded vs to stone such. What saiest thou therfore?
And this they said tempting him: that they might accuse him. But <sc>IESVS</sc> bovving him self dovvne, vvith his finger vvrote in the earth.
VVhen they therfore continued asking him: he lifted vp him self, and said to them, <na>[1]</na> He that is vvithout sinne of you, let him first throvv the stone at her.

notes.text: We can not conueniently reprehend or condemne other mens faults, if our selues be guilty of the same or other greater. Cyril in Io. See Annot. Mt. 7, 1.

verses.text: And againe bovving him self, he vvrote in the earth.
And they hearing, went out one by one, beginning at the seniours: and <sc>IESVS</sc> alone remained, and the vvoman standing in the middes.
And <sc>IESVS</sc> lifting vp him self, said to her, VVoman, vvhere are they that accused thee? hath no man condemned thee?
VVho said, No man, Lord. And <sc>IESVS</sc> said, <na>[1]</na> Neither vvil I condemne thee. Goe, and novv sinne no more. ⊢

notes.text: S. Augustine by this example of our Maister proueth that Clergie men specially should be giuen much to mercie: and that they ought often, as the cause and time require, to get pardon of the secular Magistrates for offenders that be penitent. Ep. 54.

verses.text: <na>[1]</na> b Againe <sc>therfore IESVS</sc> spake to them, saying, I am the light of the vvorld. he that folovveth me, vvalketh not in darkenesse: but shal haue the light of life.

notes.text: The Gospel vpon Saturday the 4 weeke in Lent.

verses.text: The Pharisees therfore said to him, Thou giuest testimonie of thy self: thy testimonie is not true.

<sc>IESVS</sc> ansvvered, and said to them, Although I doe giue testimonie of my self, my testimonie is true: because I knovv vvhence I came, & vvhither I goe: but you knovv not whence I come, or whither I goe.
You iudge according to the flesh: I doe not iudge any man.
And if I doe iudge, my iudgement is true: because I am not alone, but I and he that sent me, the Father.
And in your lavv it is vvritten, that <cr>[1]</cr> the testimonie of tvvo men is true.
I am he that giue testimonie of my self: and he that sent me, the Father, giueth testimonie of me.
They said therfore to him, VVhere is thy father? <sc>IESVS</sc> ansvvered, Neither me doe you knovv, nor my Father. If you did knovv me: perhaps you might knovv my Father also.
These vvordes <sc>IESVS</sc> spake in the Treasurie, teaching in the temple: and no man apprehended him, because his houre vvas not yet come. ⊢
<na>[1]</na> Againe therfore <sc>IESVS</sc> said to them, I goe, and you shal seeke me, and shal die in your sinne. VVhither I goe, you can not come.

notes.text: The Gospel vpon Munday in the 2 weeke of Lent.

verses.text: The Iewes therfore said, VVhy, vvil he kil him self, because he saith, Whither I goe, you can not come?
And he said to them, You are from beneath, I am from aboue. you are of this vvorld, I am not of this vvorld.
Therfore I said to you that you shal die in your sinnes. for if you beleeue not that I am he, you shal die in your sinne.
They said therfore to him, VVho art thou? <sc>IESVS</sc> said to them, <na>[1]</na> The beginning vvho also speake to you.

notes.text: So read S. Cyril, S. Ambrose, & S. Augustine: expounding it of Christes person, that he is the beginning or cause of al creatures.

verses.text: Many things I haue to speake and iudge of you. but he that sent me, is true: and vvhat I haue heard of him, these things I speake in the world.
And they knevv not that he said to them that his father vvas God.

<sc>IESVS</sc> therfore said to them, VVhen you shal haue exalted the sonne of man, then you shal know that I am he, and of my self I doe nothing, but as the Father hath taught me, these things I speake:
and he that sent me, is vvith me: and he hath not left me alone, because the things that please him I doe alvvaies. ⊢
When he spake these things, many beleeued in him.
<sc>IESVS</sc> therfore said to them that beleeued him, the Ievves: If you <na>[1]</na> abide in my vvorde, you shal be my disciples in deede.

notes.text: Onely faith is not sufficient without perseuêrance or abiding in the keeping of his cōmaundements.

verses.text: And you shal knovv the truth, and the truth shal make you free.
They ansvvered him, VVe are the seed of Abraham, and vve neuer serued any man: hovv saiest thou, You shal be free?
<sc>IESVS</sc> ansvvered them, Amen, amen I say to you, that <cr>[1]</cr> euery one vvhich committeth sinne, is the seruant of sinne.
and the seruant abideth not in the house for euer: the sonne abideth for euer.
If therfore the sonne make you free, you shal be <na>[1]</na> free in deede.

notes.text: Man was neuer without free wil: but hauing the grace of Christ, his wil is truely made free (as S. Augustine saith) from seruitude of sinne also. tract. 41 in Euang. Io.

verses.text: I know that you are the children of Abraham: but you seeke to kil me, because my vvorde taketh not in you.
I speake that vvhich I haue seen vvith my father: and you doe the things that you haue seen vvith your father.
They ansvvered, and said to him, Our father is Abraham. <sc>IESVS</sc> saith to them, If you be the children of Abraham, <na>[1]</na> doe the vvorkes of Abraham.

notes.text: Not onely faith but good workes also make men the children of Abraham. according as S. Iames also speaketh of Abrahams workes c. 2.

verses.text: But novv, you seeke to kil me, a man that haue spoken the truth to you, vvhich I haue heard of God. this did not Abraham.
You doe the vvorkes of your father. They said therfore to him, VVe vvere not borne of fornication. vve haue one father, God.
<sc>IESVS</sc> therfore said to them, If God vvere your father: verely you vvould loue me. for from God I proceded, and came: for I came not of my self, but he sent me:
VVhy doe you not knovv my speach? Because you can not heare my vvord.

You are of your father the Diuel, and the desires of your father you vvil doe. he vvas a <na>[1]</na> mankiller from the beginning, and he stoode not in the veritie: because veritie is not in him. vvhen he speaketh a lie, he speaketh of his owne, because he is a lyer, and the father thereof.

notes.text: S. Augustine compareth Heretikes in their spiritual murder by driuing Christian men out of the Church, to the Diuel that droue our parents out of Paradise. Cont. lit. Petil. li. 2, c. 13.

verses.text: But because I say the veritie, you beleeue me not.
VVhich of you shal argue me of sinne? If I say the veritie: why doe you not beleeue me?
<na>[1]</na> He that is of God, heareth the vvordes of God. Therfore you heare not, because you are not of God.

notes.text: The Gospel vpon PASSION Sunday.

verses.text: The Iewes therfore ansvvered, and said to him, Doe not we say vvel that thou art a Samaritane, and hast a diuil?
<sc>IESVS</sc> ansvvered, <na>[1]</na> I haue no deuil: but I doe honour my Father, and you haue dishonoured me.

notes.text: He denieth not that he is a Samaritane, because he is our keeper or protector, as the word signifieth, and because he is in deede that merciful Samaritane in the parable of the wounded man Luc. 10, 33. Aug. tract. 43 in Ioan.

verses.text: but I seeke not mine ovvne glorie. there is that seeketh and iudgeth.
Amen, amen I say to you, If any man keepe my vvord, he shal not see death for euer.
The Ievves therfore said, Now vve haue knovven that thou hast a deuil. Abraham is dead, and the Prophets: and thou saiest, If any man keepe my word, he shal not tast death for euer.
VVhy, art thou greater then our father Abraham, vvho is dead? and the Prophets are dead. VVhom doest thou make thy self?
<sc>IESVS</sc> answered, If I doe glorifie my self, my glorie is nothing. it is my father that glorifieth me, vvhom you say that he is your God.
And you haue not knovven him, but I knovv him. And if I shal say that I knovv him not: I shal be like to you, a lyer. But I doe knovv him, and doe keepe his vvord.
Abraham your father reioyced that he might see my day: and he savv, and vvas glad.
The Ievves therfore said to him, Thou hast not yet fiftie yeres, and hast thou seen Abraham?
<sc>IESVS</sc> said to them, Amen, amen I say to you, before that Abraham vvas made, I am.
They tooke stones therfore to cast at him. but <sc>IESVS</sc> hid him self, and vvent out of the temple. ⊢

chapters.summary: Againe in the Temple (absoluing an aduoutresse after his merciful maner, and yet withal declaring against his enemies that he is not a fauourer of sinne, no more then Moyses) 12 he teacheth openly, and is not for al that apprehended. telling them both of his Godhead, 21 and of their reprobation, 28 of his exaltation also by their Crucifying of him. 31 exhorting the beleeuers to perseuére: 33 and shewing them that seeke his death, that they are neither free, 39 nor of Abraham, 41 nor of God, 44 but of the Diuel. 45 but that him selfe is of God, 52 and greater and auncienter then Abraham. 59 For the which they goe about to stone him, but in vaine.

verses.text: Lord receiveth him: 39. and foretelleth by this occasion, the excecation of the Jews (because of their willful obstinacy) and illumination of the Gentiles who confess their own blindness.
<sc>AND <na>[1]</na> IESVS</sc> passing by, savv a man blinde from his natiuitie:

notes.text: The Gospel vpon wenesday in the 4 weeke of Lent.

verses.text: and his disciples asked him, Rabbi, vvho hath sinned, this man, or his parents, that he should be borne <sc>blinde</sc>?
IESVS ansvvered, <na>[1]</na> Neither hath this man sinned, nor his parents: but that the vvorkes of God may be manifested in him.

notes.text: Though many infirmities fall for sinne, yet not al. some comming for probation, and some sent that God by the cure thereof may be glorified.

verses.text: I must vvorke the vvorkes of him that sent me, vvhiles it is day. The night commeth, <na>[1]</na> vvhen no man can vvorke.

notes.text: The time of working, and meriting, is in this life: after death we can deserue no more by our deedes, but must onely receiue good or il, according to the difference of workes here.

verses.text: As long as I am in the vvorld, I am the light of the vvorld.
When he had said these things, he spit on the ground, and made clay of the spettle, and spred the clay vpon his eies,
and said to him, Goe, <na>[1]</na> c vvash in the poole of Siloé, vvhich is interpreted, Sent. He vvent therfore, and vvashed: and he came seeing.

notes.text: This was a figure of Baptisme, to which al men borne in sinne and blindnes are sent for health & sight. Ambr. li. 3 c. 2 de Sacramentis.

verses.text: Therfore the neighbours, and they vvhich had seen him before, that he vvas a begger, said, Is not this he that sate, and begged?
Others said, That this is he. But others, No, not so, but he is like him. But he said, That I am he.
They said therfore to him, Hovv vvere thine eies opened?
He answered, That man that is called <sc>IESVS</sc>, made clay: and anointed mine eies, and said to me, Goe to the poole of Siloé, and wash. And I vvent, and vvashed, and savv.
And they said to him, VVhere is he? He saith, I know not.
They bring him that had been blinde, to the Pharisees.
And it vvas the Sabboth when <sc>IESVS</sc> made the clay, and opened his eies.
Againe therfore the Pharisees asked him, hovv he savv. But he said to them, He put clay vpon mine eies, & I vvashed: and I see.
Certaine therfore of the Pharisees said, This man is not of God, that keepeth not the Sabboth. But others said, Hovv can a man that is a sinner doe these signes? And there vvas a schisme among them.
They say therfore to the blinde againe, Thou, vvhat saiest thou of him that opened thine eies? And he said, That he is a Prophet.
The Ievves therfore did not beleeue of him, that he had been blinde and savv: vntil they called the parents of him that savv,
and asked them, saying, Is this your sonne, vvhom you say that he vvas borne blinde? hovv then doeth he now see?
His parents ansvvered them, and said, VVe know that this is our sonne, and that he vvas borne blinde:
but hovv he now seeth, vve knovv not, or vvho hath opened his eies, we knovv not, aske him self: he is of age, let him self speake of him self.
These things his parents said, because they feared the Ievves. for the Ievves had now conspired, that if any man should confesse him to be <sc>CHRIST</sc>, he should be put out of the Synagogue.
Therfore did his parents say, That he is of age, aske him self.
They therfore againe called the man that had been blinde, and said to him, <na>[1]</na> Giue glorie to God. vve knovv that this man is a sinner.

notes.text: So say the Heretikes when they derogat from miracles done by Saincts or their Relikes, pharisaically pretending the glorie of God. As though it were not Gods glorie, when his Saincts do it by his power and vertue: yea his greater glorie, that doeth such things by his seruants, & by the meanest things belonging to them, as Peters shadow Act. 5. & Paules napkin Act. 9.

verses.text: He therfore said to them, Whether he be a sinner, I know not: one thing I know, that vvhereas I vvas blinde, novv I see.
They said therfore to him, VVhat did he to thee? hovv did he open thine eies?
He ansvvered them, I haue now told you, and you haue heard: vvhy vvil you heare it againe? vvil you also become his disciples?
They reuiled him therfore, & said, Be thou his disciple: but we are the disciples of Moyses.
VVe know that to Moyses God did speake: but this man vve knovv not vvhence he is.
The man ansvvered and said to them, For in this it is marueilous that you knovv not vvhence he is, and he hath opened mine eies.
and vve know that sinners God doth not heare. but if a man be a seruer of God, and doe the vvil of him, him he heareth.
From the beginning of the vvorld it hath not been heard that any man hath opened the eies of one borne blinde.
Vnles this man vvere of God, he could not doe any thing.
They ansvvered, and said to him, Thou wast wholy borne in sinnes, and doest thou teach vs? And they did cast him forth.
<sc>IESVS</sc> heard that they cast him forth: and vvhen he had found him, he said to him, Doest thou beleeue in the sonne of God?
He ansvvered, and said, VVho is he Lord, that I may beleeue in him?
And <sc>IESVS</sc> said to him, Both thou hast seen him: and he that talketh vvith thee, he it is.
But he said, I beleeue Lord. And falling dovvne he adored him. ⊢
And <sc>IESVS</sc> said to him, For iudgement came I into this vvorld: <na>[1]</na> that they that see not, may see: and they that see, may become blinde.

notes.text: By this we see that this miracle was not onely maruelous and beneficial to the blinde, but also significatiue of taking away spiritual blindnesse.

verses.text: And certaine of the Pharisees that vvere vvith him, heard: and they said to him, VVhy, are vve also blinde?
<sc>IESVS</sc> said to them, If you vvere blinde, you should not haue sinne. but novv you say, That vve see. Your sinne remaineth.

chapters.summary: To show that by his Baptisme (being the Sacrament of illumination or faith) he wil take away the blindnes of the world, he giueth with strange ceremonies sight to one borne blinde. 8 By which wonderful miracle (the attestation of the partie him self and of his parents concurring) first the neighbours, then also the Pharisees them selues are plainely confounded. Yet so obstinate they are, that because it was the Sabboth when he wrought it, they inferre that he is not of God: yea and throw out of their Synagogue the partie for confessing him. 35 But our Lord receiueth him: 39 and foretelleth by this occasion, the excecation of the Iewes (because of their wilful obstinacie) and illumination of the Gentils who confesse their owne blindnes.

verses.text: <sc>AMEN</sc>, <na>[1]</na> amen I say to you, he that entreth not by the doore into the folde of the sheepe, but climeth vp an other vvay: he is <na>[2]</na> a theefe and a robber.

notes.text: The Gospel vpon Tuesday in whitson weeke.
The theefe, is the Heretike specially, & any other that vnlawfully breake in vpon the sheepe to kil & destroy them by false doctrine and otherwise.

verses.text: But he that entreth by the doore, is the Pastor of the sheepe.
To this man the porter openeth: & the sheepe heare his voice: and he calleth his ovvne sheepe by name, and leadeth them forth.
And vvhen he hath let forth his ovvne sheepe, he <na>[1]</na> goeth before them: and the sheepe folovv him, because they knovv his voice.

notes.text: That is the fashion of Iewrie & other countries, signifying that the shepheard or Pastor must teach the sheepe, and not they him.

verses.text: But a stranger they folovv not, but flee from him: because they knovv not the voice of strangers.
This prouerbe <sc>IESVS</sc> said to them. But they knew not vvhat he spake to them.
<sc>IESVS</sc> therfore said to them againe, Amen, amen I say to you, that I am the doore of the sheepe.
And hovv many soeuer haue come, are theeues and robbers: but the sheepe heard them not.
I am the doore. By me if any enter, he shal be saued: and he shal goe in and shal goe out, and shal finde pastures.
The theefe commeth not but to steale and kil and destroy. I came that they may haue life, and may haue more aboundantly. ⊢
<na>[1]</na> I am the good Pastor.

notes.text: The Gospel upon the 2. Sunday after Easter, & for S. Thomas of Canterburie. Decemb. 29. And in his Translation. Iulij. 7.

verses.text: <cr>[1]</cr> But the hireling and he that is not the Pastor, vvhose ovvne the sheepe are not, seeth the vvoulfe comming, and leaueth the sheepe, and fleeth: and the woulfe raueneth, and disperseth the sheepe.
And the hireling fleeth because he is a hireling: and he hath no care of the sheepe.
I am the good Pastor: and I knovv mine, and mine knovv me.
As the Father knovveth me, and I knovv the Father: and <na>[1]</na> I yeld my life for my sheepe.

notes.text: Christes death was so necessarie for the flocke, that when he might haue escaped, he voluntarily offered him self to death for his flocke.

verses.text: And c other sheepe I haue that are not of this folde: them also I must bring, and they shal heare my voice, and there shal be made <cr>[1]</cr> one folde and one Pastor. ⊢
<na>[1]</na> Therfore the Father loueth me: because I yeld my life, that I may take it againe.

notes.text: He meaneth the Church of the Gentils.

verses.text: No man taketh it avvay from me: but <cr>[1]</cr> I yeld it of my self. and I haue povver to yeld it: and I haue povver to take it againe. This commaundement I receiued of my father.
A dissension rose againe among the Ievves for these vvordes.
And many of them said, He hath a deuil and is mad: vvhy heare you him?
Others said, These are not the vvordes of one that hath a deuil. can a deuil open the eies of blinde men?
<cr>[1]</cr> And the Dedication vvas in Hierusalem: and it vvas vvinter.
<na>[1]</na> And <sc>IESVS</sc> vvalked in the temple, in Salomons porche.

notes.text: The Gospel vpon Wenesday in Passion weeke.

verses.text: The Ievves therfore compassed him round about, and said to him, Hovv long doest thou hold our soule in suspense? if thou be <sc>CHRIST</sc>, tel vs openly.
<sc>IESVS</sc> answered them, I speake to you: and you beleeue not. the vvorkes that I doe in the name of my Father, they giue testimonie of me.
but you doe not beleeue, because you are not of my sheepe.
My sheepe heare my voice: and I knovv them, and they folovv me.
And I giue them life euerlasting: and they shal not perish for euer, and no man shal plucke them out of my hand.
<na>[1]</na> My father, that vvhich he hath giuen me, is greater then al: and no man can plucke them out of the hand of my father.

notes.text: An other reading is, My father that hath giuen me, &c.

verses.text: I and the Father are c <na>[1]</na> one.

notes.text: c unum.

verses.text: The Ievves tooke vp stones, to stone him.
<sc>IESVS</sc> ansvvered them, Many good vvorkes I haue shewed you from my father, for vvhich of those vvorkes doe you stone me?
The Iewes ansvvered him, For a good vvorke we stone the not, but for blasphemie, and because thou being a man, makest thy self God.
IESVS ansvvered them, Is it not written in your lavv, that I said, you are goddes? [1]
If he called them goddes, to vvhom the vvord of God vvas made, and the scripture can not be broken:
vvhom the Father hath sanctified and sent into the vvorld, say you, That thou blasphemest, because I said I am the sonne of God?
If I doe not the vvorkes of my father, beleeue me not.
But if I doe, and if you vvil not beleeue me, beleeue the vvorkes: that you may knovv and beleeue that the Father is in me, and I in the Father. ⊢
They sought therfore to apprehend him: and he vvent forth out of their handes.
and he vvent againe beyond Iordan into that place vvhere Iohn vvas baptizing first: and he taried there.
and many came to him. and they said, That Iohn in deede did no signe. But al things vvhatsoeuer Iohn said of this man, vvere true.
And many beleeued in him.

chapters.summary: He continueth his talke to the Pharisees; shewing that they and al other that wil not enter in by him, are wolues: and that they which heare them, are not the true sheepe. 11 But that him self is the good Pastor, and therfore to saue the sheepe from these wolues, he wil yeld his life, which otherwise no might of theirs could take from him: foretelling also his Resurrection, and vocation of the Gentils. 22 Againe an other time, he telleth these Iewes openly, that they are not of his sheepe, and that no might of theirs shal take from him his true sheepe, because he is God, euen as his Father is God. 31 Which by his miracles and by Scripture he sheweth to be no blasphemie: and they in vaine seeking to stone and to apprehend him, 40 he goeth out to the place where Iohn Baptist had giuen open witnes of him.

verses.text: <sc>AND</sc> <na>[1]</na> there vvas a certaine sicke man, Lazarus of Bethánia, of the tovvne of Marie and Martha her sister.

notes.text: The Gospel vpon Friday in the 4 weeke of Lent.

verses.text: (And Marie vvas she <cr>[1]</cr> that anointed our Lord vvith ointement, and vviped his feete vvith her heare: vvhose brother Lazarus vvas sicke.)
His sisters therfore sent to him saying, Lord, behold, he vvhom thou louest, is sicke.
And <sc>IESVS</sc> hearing, said to them, This sicknesse is not to death, but for the glorie of God: that the sonne of God may be glorified by it.
And <sc>IESVS</sc> loued Martha, and her sister Marie, and Lazarus.
As he heard therfore that he vvas sicke, then he taried in the same place tvvo daies:
then after this he saith to his Disciples, Let vs goe into Ievvrie againe.
The Disciples say to him, Rabbi, now the Ievves sought to stone thee: and goest thou thither againe?
<sc>IESVS</sc> answered, Are there not tvvelue houres of the day? If a man vvalke in the day, he stumbleth not: because he seeth the light of this world:
but if he walke in the night, he stumbleth, because the light is not in him.
These things he said: and after this he saith to them, Lazarus our frende sleepeth: but I goe that I may raise him from sleepe.
His Disciples therfore said, Lord, if he sleepe, he shal be safe.
but <sc>IESVS</sc> spake of his death: & they thought that he spake c <na>[1]</na> of the sleeping of sleepe.

notes.text: de dormitione somni.

verses.text: Then therfore <sc>IESVS</sc> said to them plainely, Lazarus is dead:
and I am glad for your sake, that you may beleeue, because I vvas not there. but let vs goe to him.
Thomas therfore, vvho is called Didymus, said to his condisciples, Let vs also goe, to die vvith him.
<sc>IESVS</sc> therfore came, and found him now hauing been foure daies in the graue.
(and Bethánia vvas nigh to Hierusalem about fiftene furlonges.)
And many of the Ievves vvere come to Martha and Marie, to comfort them concerning theire brother.
Martha therfore vvhen she heard that <sc>IESVS</sc> vvas come, vvent to meete him: but Marie sat at home.
<na>[1]</na> Martha therfore said to <sc>IESVS</sc>, Lord if thou hadst been here, my brother had not died.
