notes.text: The Gospel in a Masse for the dead vpon the day of the burial or deposition.

verses.text: but novv also I knovv that vvhat things soeuer thou shalt aske of God, God vvil giue thee.
<sc>IESVS</sc> saith to her, Thy brother shal rise againe.
Martha saith to him, I know that he shal rise againe in the resurrection, in the last day.
<sc>IESVS</sc> said to her, I am the resurrection and the life: he that beleeueth in me, although he be dead, shal liue.
and euery one that liueth, and beleeueth in me, shal not die for euer, Beleeuest thou this?
She saith to him, Yea Lord, I haue beleeued that thou art <sc>CHRIST</sc> the sonne of God that art come into this vvorld. ⊢
And vvhen she had said these things, she went, and called Marie her sister secretely, saying, The maister is come, & calleth thee.
She, when she heard, riseth quickely, & commeth to him.
For <sc>IESVS</sc> was not yet come into the towne: but he vvas yet in that place vvhere Martha had mette him.

The Ievves therfore that vvere vvith her in the house and did comfort her, vvhen they savv Marie that she rose quickly and vvent forth, folovved her, saying, That she goeth to the graue, to vveepe there.
Marie therfore vvhen she vvas come vvhere <sc>IESVS</sc> vvas, seeing him, fel at his feete, and saith to him, Lord, if thou hadst been here, my brother had not died.
<sc>IESVS</sc> therfore vvhen he savv her vveeping, and the Ievves that vvere come vvith her, vveeping, he groned in spirit, and troubled him self,
and said, VVhere haue you laid him? They say to him, Lord, come and see.
And <sc>IESVS</sc> vvept.
The Ievves therfore said, Behold hovv he loued him.
But certaine of them said, Could not he that <cr>[1]</cr> opened the eies of the blinde man, make that this man should not die?
<sc>IESVS</sc> therfore againe groning in him self, commeth to the graue. and it vvas a caue: and a stone vvas laid ouer it.
<sc>IESVS</sc> saith, Take avvay the stone. Martha the sister of him that vvas dead, saith to him, Lord, novv he stinketh, for he is novv of foure daies.
<sc>IESVS</sc> saith to her, Did not I say to thee, that if thou beleeue, thou shalt see the glorie of God?
They tooke therfore the stone avvay. And <sc>IESVS</sc> lifting his eies vpvvard, said, Father, I giue thee thankes that thou hast heard me.
and I did know that thou doest alvvaies heare me, but for the people that standeth about, haue I said it, that they may beleeue that thou hast sent me.
VVhen he had said these things, he cried vvith a loude voice, Lazarus, come forth.

And forthvvith he came forth that had been dead, bound feete and handes vvith vvinding bandes, and his face vvas tied vvith a napkin. <sc>IESVS</sc> said to them, <na>[1]</na> Loose him, and let him goe.

notes.text: S. Cyril li. 7 c. vlt. in Io. and S. August. Tract. 49 in Io. apply this to the Apostles and Priests authoritie of absoluing sinners: affirming Christ to reuiue none from sinne, but in the Church and by the Priests ministerie.

verses.text: Many therfore of the Ievves that vvere come to Marie and Martha, and had seen the things that <sc>IESVS</sc> did, beleeued in him. ⊢
And certaine of them vvent to the Pharisees, and told them the things that <sc>IESVS</sc> did.
<na>[1]</na> The cheefe priests therfore and the pharisees gathered a councel, and said, VVhat doe vve, for this man doeth many signes.

notes.text: The Gospel vpon friday in Passion weeke.

verses.text: If we let him alone so, al vvil beleeue in him: and the Romanes vvil come, and <na>[1]</na> take avvay our place and nation.

notes.text: Al men, but specially Nations must take heede, that whiles to saue their temporal state, they forsake God: they lose not both as the Iewes did. Aug. tract. 49 in Io.

verses.text: But one of them named Caiphas, being the high priest of that yere, said to them, You knovv nothing,
neither doe you consider that it is expedient for vs that one man die for the people, and the vvhole nation perish not.
And this he said not of him self: but being the high priest of that yere, he prophecied that <sc>IESVS</sc> should die for the nation:
and not only for the nation, but to gather into one the children of God that vvere dispersed.
From that day therfore they deuised to kil him.
<sc>IESVS</sc> therfore vvalked no more openly among the Ievves, but he vvent into the countrie beside the desert vnto a citie that is called Ephrem, and there he abode vvith his Disciples. ⊢
And the Pasche of the Ievves vvas at hand: and many of the countrie vvent vp to Hierusalem before the Pasche to sanctifie them selues.

They sought <sc>IESVS</sc> therfore: and they communed one vvith an other, standing in the temple, VVhat thinke you, in that he is not come to the festiual day? And the cheefe Priests & Pharisees had giuen commaundement, that if any man should knovv vvhere he vvas, he should tel, that they might apprehend him.

chapters.summary: He commeth once againe into Iewrie boldly (the time that he would be killed of them, being not yet come) and raiseth Lazarus foure daies buried. 47. At which miracle the blind malice of the rulers so increaseth, that in Councel they conclude to make him away. howbeit the high Priest prophecieth vnawares, of the saluation of the world by his death. 54 He therevpon goeth againe out of the way.

verses.text: <sc>IESVS</sc> <cr>[1]</cr><na>[2]</na> therfore sixe daies before the Pasche came to Bethánia, vvhere Lazarus vvas, that had been dead, vvhom <sc>IESVS</sc> raised.

notes.text: The Gospel vpō Munday in Holy weeke.

verses.text: <na>[1]</na> And they made him a supper there: and Martha ministred, but Lazarus vvas one of them that sate at the table vvith him.

notes.text: PALME SVNDAY eue.

verses.text: <na>[1]</na> Marie therfore tooke a pownd of ointement of right spikenard, pretious, and anointed the feete of <sc>IESVS</sc>, and vviped his feete with her heare: and the house vvas filled of the odour of the ointment.

notes.text: Of this womans extraordinarie offices of deuotion, & how acceptable they were to Christ, see the Annot. Mt. 26.

verses.text: One therfore of his disciples, Iudas Iscariote, he that vvas to betray him, said,
VVhy vvas not this ointment sold for three-hundred pence, and giuen to the poore?
And he said this, not because he cared for the poore: but because he vvas a theefe, and hauing the purse, caried the things that vvere put in.
<sc>IESVS</sc> therfore said, Let her alone that she may keepe it for the day of my <na>[1]</na> burial.

notes.text: The devout offices of balming and anointing the dead

verses.text: For the poore you haue alvvaies vvith you: but <na>[1]</na> me you shal not haue alwaies.

notes.text: Not in visible and mortal cōdition, to receiue almes of you or such like offices for supply of my necessities.

verses.text: A great multitude therfore of the Ievves knevv that he vvas there: and they came, not for <sc>IESVS</sc> only, but that they might see Lazarus, vvhom he raised from the dead. ⊢
But the cheefe Priests deuised for to kil Lazarus also:
<na>[1]</na> because many for him of the Ievves vvent avvay, and beleeued in <sc>IESVS</sc>.

notes.text: The Gospel vpon Saturday in Passion weeke.

verses.text: And on the morow a great multitude that vvas come to the festiual day, <na>[1]</na> vvhen they had heard that <sc>IESVS</sc> commeth to Hierusalem:

notes.text: PALME SVNDAY.

verses.text: they tooke the [1] boughes of palmes, and vvent forth to meete him, and cried, Hosanna, blessed is he that commeth in the name of our Lord, the king of Israel. [2]
And <sc>IESVS</sc> found a yong asse, and sate vpon it, as it is vvritten,
Feare not daughter of Sion: behold, thy king commeth sitting vpon an asses colt. [1]
These things his disciples did not knovv at the first: but vvhen <sc>IESVS</sc> vvas glorified, then they remembred that these things had been vvritten of him, and these things they did to him.
The multitude therfore gaue testimonie, vvhich vvas vvith him when he called Lazarus out of the graue, and raised him from the dead.
For therfore also the multitude came to meete him, because they heard that he had done this signe.
The Pharisees therfore said among them selues, Doe you see that vve preuaile nothing? behold, the vvhole vvorld is gone after him.
And there vvere certaine Gentiles of them that <na>[1]</na> came vp to adore in the festiual day.

notes.text: We may see there is a great difference where a man pray or adore, at home or in the Church & holy places: when the Gentils also came of deuotion a pilgrimage to the Temple in Hierusalem.

verses.text: These therfore came to Philippe vvho vvas of Bethsaida of Galilee, and desired him, saying, Sir, vve are desirous to see <sc>IESVS</sc>.
Philippe commeth, and telleth Andrevv. Againe Andrevv & Philippe told <sc>IESVS</sc>.
But <sc>IESVS</sc> ansvvered them, saying, The houre is come, that the Sonne of man shal be glorified.
b <na>[1]</na> Amen, amen I say to you, vnles the graine of vvheate falling into the ground, die: it self remaineth alone. but if it die, it bringeth much fruite.

notes.text: b The Gospel for S. Ignatius Febr. 1. And S. Laurence Aug. 10. And for some other martyrs not Bishops.

verses.text: He that loueth his life, shal lose it: and he that hateth his life in this vvorld, doth keepe it to life euerlasting.
If any man minister to me, let him folovv me: and vvhere I am, there also shal my minister be. If any man minister to me, my father vvil honour him. ⊢
Novv my soule is troubled. And vvhat shal I say? Father, saue me from this houre. But therfore came I into this houre.
Father, glorifie thy name. A voice therfore came from heauen, Both I haue glorified it, and againe I vvil glorifie it.
The multitude therfore that stoode and had heard, said that it thundered. Others said, An Angel spake to him.
<sc>IESVS</sc> ansvvered, and said, This voice came not for me, but for your sake.
<na>[1]</na> Novv is the iudgement of the vvorld: novv the Prince of this vvorld shal be cast forth.

notes.text: The Gospel vpon Holy roode day Septemb. 14. in latin, Exaltatio S. Crucis.

verses.text: And I, <cr>[1]</cr> if I be exalted from the earth, vvil dravv al things to my self.
(and this he said, signifying vvhat death he should die.)
The multitude ansvvered him, VVe haue heard out of the lavv, that <sc>CHRIST</sc> abideth for euer: and hovv saiest thou, The Sonne of man must be exalted? VVho is this Sonne of man?

<sc>IESVS</sc> therfore said to them, Yet a litle vvhile, the light is among you. VValke vvhiles you haue the light, that the darkenesse ouertake you not. And he that vvalketh in darkenesse, knovveth not vvhither he goeth.
VVhiles you haue the light, beleeue in the light, that you may be the children of light. ⊢ These things <sc>IESVS</sc> spake and he vvent avvay, and hid him self from them. ⊢
And whereas he had done so many signes before them, they beleeued not in him:
that the saying of Esay the Prophet might be fulfilled, vvhich he said, Lord, vvho hath beleeued the hearing of vs? and the arme of our Lord to whom hath it bene reuealed? [1]
Therfore they <na>[1]</na> could not beleeue, because Esay said againe,

notes.text: If any man aske (saith S. Augustine) why they could not beleeue: I answer roundly, because they would not. Tract. 33. in Io. See the meaning of this speach Annot. Mat. 13, 15. Mar. 4, 12.

verses.text: He hath blinded their eies, and indurated their hart: that they may not see vvith their eies, nor vnderstand vvith their hart, and be conuerted, and I heale them. [1]
These things said Esaie, vvhen he savv his glorie, and spake of him.
But yet of the Princes also many beleeued in him: but <na>[1]</na> for the Pharisees they did not confesse, that they might not be cast out of the Synagogue.

notes.text: This is the case of many principal men in such countries where heresie hath the vpperhand, who know and beleeue the Catholike faith: but making choise rather to keepe mans fauour then Gods, they dare not confesse the same. Such may pray that God and the world agree together: for els it is seen whose part they wil take.

verses.text: for they loued the glorie of men more, then the glorie of God.
But <sc>IESVS</sc> cried, and said, He that beleeueth in me, doth not beleeue in me, but in him that sent me.
And he that seeth me, seeth him that sent me.
I a light am come into this vvorld: that euery one vvhich beleeueth in me, may not remaine in the darkenesse.
And if any man heare my wordes, and keepe them not: I doe not iudge him. for I came not to iudge the vvorld, but to saue the vvorld.
He that despiseth me, & receiueth not my vvordes, hath that iudgeth him. the vvord that I haue spoken, that shal iudge him in the last day.
Because of my self I haue not spoken, but the Father that sent me, he gaue me commaundement vvhat I should say, and what I should speake.
And I knovv that his commaundement is life euerlasting. The things therfore that I speake: as the Father said to me, so doe I speake.

chapters.summary: The Rulers dealing as if he hid him self, 1 he commeth to Bethania, 3 Where by occasion of Iudas the theefe murmuring at Marie Magdalens costly deuotion, he foretelleth his death. 12 From thence, though they did now intend to kil Lazarus also, he rideth openly into Hierusalem, the people (because he had raised Lazarus) confessing with their acclamations that he is Christ. 20 Where certaine Gentils desiring to see him, 23 he foretelleth the conuersion of the whole world from the Diuel to him, to be now instant, as the effect of his death vpon the Crosse. 28 The Father also answering from heauen to his prayer made to that purpose, 37 yet after al this, the Iewes continew incredulous as Esay prophecied of them: 42 though many beleeued, but were ashamed to confesse him. 44 Wherevpon he sheweth that it is glorious before God, and saluation to them selues, to beleeue in him, and confesse him: and damnable, to despise him. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text: The 4. part. THE 4 Pasch, & Holy Week of his Passion in Hierusalem.

verses.text: Peter who presumed too much of his own strength, that even this night he will deny him thrice.

<sc>AND</sc> <cr>[1]</cr><na>[2]</na> before the festiual day of Pasche, <sc>IESVS</sc> knovving that his houre was come that he should passe out of this vvorld to his Father: vvhereas he had loued his that vvere in the vvorld, vnto the end he loued them. <na>[3]</na>

notes.text: The Gospel vpon Maundy thursday at Masse, and at the washing of feete.
MAVNDY THVRSDAY.

verses.text: And when <na>[1]</na> supper was done, vvhereas the deuil novv had put into the hart of Iudas Iscariote the sonne of Simon, to betray him:

notes.text: By supper, he meaneth the eating of the Paschal lambe. for, the institution of the B. Sacrament was after this.

verses.text: knowing that the Father gaue him al things into his handes, and that he came from God, and goeth to God:
he riseth from supper, and laieth aside his garments, and hauing taken a tovvel, girded him self.
After that, he put vvater into a bason, and began to vvash the feete of the disciples, and to vvipe them vvith the tovvel vvherevvith he vvas girded.
He commeth therfore to Simon Peter. And Peter saith to him, Lord, doest thou vvash my feete?
<sc>IESVS</sc> ansvvered and said to him, That vvhich I doe, thou knovvest not novv, hereafter thou shalt knovv.
Peter saith to him, Thou shalt not wash my feete for euer. <sc>IESVS</sc> ansvvered him, If I wash thee not, thou shalt not haue part with me.
Simon Peter saith to him, Lord, not only my feete, but also handes, and head.
<sc>IESVS</sc> saith to him, He that is vvashed, nedeeth not but to wash his feete, but is cleane vvholy. And you are cleane, but not al.
For he knevv vvho he vvas that vvould betray him. therfore he said, You are not cleane al.
Therfore, after he had vvashed their feete, and taken his garments, being set dovvne, againe he said to them, Knovv you what I haue done to you?
You cal me, Maister, and Lord: and you say vvel, for I am so.
If then I haue washed your feete, Lord and Maister, you also ought to wash one an others feete.
For I haue giuen you an example, that as I haue done to you, so you doe also. ⊢
Amen, amen I say to you, a seruant is not greater then his lord, neither is an apostle greater then he that sent him.
If you know these things, you shal be blessed if you doe them.
I speake not of you al: I know vvhom I haue chosen. But that the scripture may be fulfilled, He that eateth bread vvith me, shal lift vp his heele against me. [1]
From this time I tel you, before it come to passe: that vvhen it shal come to passe, you may beleeue, that I am he.
Amen, amen, I say to you, he that receiueth any that I send, receiueth me: & he that receiueth me, receiueth him that sent me.
When <sc>IESVS</sc> had said these things, he vvas troubled in spirit: and he protested, and said: <cr>[1]</cr> Amen, amen I say to you: that one of you shal betray me.
The disciples therfore looked one vpon an other, doubting of whom he spake.
There vvas therfore one of his disciples leaning in the bosome of <sc>IESVS</sc>, he whom <sc>IESVS</sc> loued.
Therfore Simon Peter beckeneth to him, and said to him, who is it of whom he speaketh?
He therfore leaning vpon the breast of <sc>IESVS</sc>, saith to him, Lord, vvho is he?
<sc>IESVS</sc> ansvvered: He it is to whom I shal reach the dipped bread. And vvhen he had dipped the bread, he gaue it to Iudas Iscariote Simons sonne.
And after the morsel, then Satan entred into him. And <sc>IESVS</sc> saith to him, That vvhich thou doest, doe it quickely.
But no man knevv of those that sate at table to vvhat purpose he said this vnto him.

For certaine thought, because Iudas had the <na>[1]</na> purse, that <sc>IESVS</sc> had said to him, Bie those things vvhich are needeful for vs to the festiual day: or that he should giue some thing to the poore.

notes.text: Christ had some prouision before hand giuen him by the Collections of the faithful, which was vsed both in his owne necessities, & bestowed vpon the poore.

verses.text: He therfore hauing receiued the morsel, incontinent vvent forth. And it vvas night.
VVhen he therfore vvas gone forth, <sc>IESVS</sc> said, Novv the Sonne of man is glorified, and God is glorified in him.
If God be glorified in him, God also vvil glorifie him in him self, and incontinent vvil he glorifie him.
Litle children, yet a litle vvhile I am vvith you. You shal seeke me, & <cr>[1]</cr> as I said to the Iewes, VVhither I goe, you can not come: to you also I say novv.
<cr>[1]</cr> A nevv commaundement I giue to you, That you loue one an other: as I haue loued you, that you also loue one an other.
In this al men shal knovv that you are my disciples, if you haue loue one to an other.
Simon Peter saith to him, Lord, vvhither goest thou? <sc>IESVS</sc> ansvvered, vvhither I goe, thou canst not now folow me, but hereafter thou shalt folow.
Peter saith to him, VVhy can not I folow thee novv? <cr>[1]</cr> I vvil yeld my life for thee.
<sc>IESVS</sc> answered him, Thy life wilt thou yeld for me? Amen, amen I say to thee, the cocke shal not crovv, vntil thou denie me thrise.

chapters.summary: At his last supper, to giue his farewel, and that in most wonderful louing maner, 4 he washeth his Disciples feete, 6 beginning with Peter, 8 (shewing how necessarie it is for vs to be washed by him in Baptisme, and needful also after Baptisme) 12 and by this example teaching them al humilitie one toward an other. 21 Then he foretelleth, that (notwithstanding his exceding loue toward them) one euen of them wil betray him, meaning Iudas, 22 as to Iohn he secretly sheweth. After whose going out, he reioyceth and saith that euen now the houre is come, 34 commendeth vnto them to loue together, as a new commaundement, 36 and foretelleth Peter who presumed to much of his owne strength, that euen this night he wil deny him thrise.

verses.text: <sc>LET</sc> <na>[1]</na> not your hart be troubled. You beleeue in God, beleeue in me also.

notes.text: The Gospel vpon SS. Philip and Iacobs day Maij. 1.

verses.text: In my fathers house there be <na>[1]</na> many mansions. If not, I vvould haue told you, Because I goe to prepare you a place.

notes.text: These mansions signifie differences of glorie in heauen. Hiero. li. 2. adu. Iouin.

verses.text: And if I goe, and prepare you a place: I come againe and vvil take you to my self, that vvhere I am, you also may be.
And vvhither I goe you knovv, and the vvay you knovv.
Thomas saith to him, Lord, vve knovv not vvhither thou goest: and hovv can vve knovv the vvay?
<sc>IESVS</sc> saith to him, I am the vvay, and the veritie, and the life. no man commeth to the Father, but by me.
If you had knovven me, my father also certes you had knovven: and from hence forth you <na>[1]</na> <alt>‘shal know</alt>’ him, and you haue seen him.

notes.text: do know

verses.text: Philippe saith to him, Lord shew vs the Father, and it sufficeth vs.
<sc>IESVS</sc> saith to him, So long time I am vvith you: & haue you not knowen me? Philippe, he that seeth me, seeth the Father also. Hovv saiest thou, Shevv vs the father?
<na>[1]</na> Doest thou not beleeue that I am in the Father, & the Father in me? The vvordes that I speake to you, of my self I speake not. But my father that abideth in me, he doeth the vvorkes.

notes.text: do ye not believe.

verses.text: Beleeue you not, that I am in the Father and the Father in me? Otherwise for the vvorkes them selues beleeue.
Amen, amen I say to you, he that beleeueth in me, the vvorkes that I doe, he also shal doe, and greater then these shal he doe,
because I goe to the Father, and vvhatsoeuer you shal aske in my name, that wil I doe: ⊢ that the Father may be glorified in the Sonne.
<na>[1]</na> If you aske me any thing in my name, that wil I doe.

notes.text: The Gospel in a votiue Masse for the election of the Pope, & vpon Whitsun eue.

verses.text: If you <na>[1]</na> loue me, keepe my commaundements.

notes.text: It is then possible both to loue Christ, and to keepe his cōmaundements.

verses.text: And I wil aske the father, and he vvil giue you an other c <na>[1]</na> Paraclete, that he may abide vvith you for euer,

notes.text: Paraclete by interpretation is either a comforter, or an aduocate: and therfore to translate it by any one of them only, is ꝑhaps to abridge the sense of this place.

verses.text: the Spirit of truth, vvhom the vvorld can not receiue, because it seeth him not, neither knovveth him, but you <na>[1]</na> <alt>‘know</alt>’ him: because he shal abide vvith you, and shal be in you.

notes.text: ‘shal knovv

verses.text: I wil not leaue you orphanes: I wil come to you.
Yet a litle vvhile: and the vvorld seeth me no more. But you see me: because I liue, and you shal liue. ⊢
In that day you shal knovv that I am in my father, and you in me, and I in you.
He that hath my commaundements, and keepeth them: he it is that loueth me. And he that loueth me, shal be loued of my father: and I vvil loue him, and vvil manifest my self to him. ⊢
Iudas saith to him, not that Iscariote, Lord, vvhat is done, that thou vvilt manifest thy self to vs, and not to the world?
<na>[1]</na> <sc>IESVS</sc> ansvvered, and said to him, If any loue me, he vvil keepe my vvord, and my father vvil loue him, and vve vvil come to him, and vvil make abode vvith him.

notes.text: The Gospel vpon Whitsunday. And in a Votiue Masse of the holy Ghost.

verses.text: He that loueth me not, keepeth not my vvordes. And the vvord vvhich you haue heard, is not mine: but his that sent me, the Fathers.
These things haue I spoken to you abiding vvith you.
But the Paraclete the holy Ghost, vvhom the Father vvil send in my name, he shal <na>[1]</na> teach you al things, & suggest vnto you al things vvhatsoeuer I shal say to you.

notes.text: See the Annot. vpon the 16 Chap. vs. 12 & 13.

verses.text: Peace I leaue to you, my peace I giue to you. not as the vvorld giueth, doe I giue to you. Let not your hart be troubled, nor feare.
You haue heard that I said to you, I goe and I come to you. If you loued me, you would be glad verily, that I goe to the Father: because the Father is greater then I.
And novv I haue told you before it come to passe: that vvhen it shal come to passe, you may beleeue.
Novv I vvil not speake many things vvith you. for the prince of this vvorld commeth, and in me he hath not any thing.
But that the vvorld may knovv that I loue the Father: and as the Father hath giuen me commaundement, so doe I: ⊢ Arise, let vs goe hence.

chapters.summary: They being sad, because he said that he must goe from them, he comforteth them many waies, as, putting them in hope to folow him vnto the same place, so that they keepe his commaundements. Where he telleth them, that him self is the way thither according to his Humanitie, and also the end according to his Diuinitie, no lesse then his Father, because he is consubstantial. 15 promising also to send vnto them (that is, to his Church) the Holy Ghost to be after his departure with them for euer. 28 And saying that it is his promotion (according to his Humanitie) to goe to the Father, for, whose obedience this his death shalbe, & not for any guilt of his owne.

verses.text: I <na>[1]</na><na>[2]</na> AM the true vine: and my father is the husband-man.

notes.text: The Gospel for some Martyrs, between Easter & Whitsunday. And on SS. Simon and Jude's eve. Oct. 27.
The Gospel upon S. George's day: April. 23. And for some other Martyrs between Easter & Whitsunday.

verses.text: Euery <na>[1]</na> branche in me, not bearing fruite, he wil take it away: and euery one that beareth fruite, he wil purge it, <na>[2]</na> that it may bring more fruite.

notes.text: Christ hath some branches in his body mystical that be fruitles. therfore il liuers also may be members of Christ & the Church.
Man may cōtinually increase in iustice and sanctification, so long as he liueth.

verses.text: Now you are cleane for the <na>[1]</na> word which I haue spoken to you.

notes.text: S. Augustine expoundeth it of the Sacramētal word of Baptisme, and not as Heretikes do, of preaching onely. Tract. 80. in Io.

verses.text: Abide in me: and I in you. As the branche can not beare fruite of it self, vnles it abide in the vine: so you neither, vnles you abide in me.
I am the vine: you the branches. he that abideth in me, and I in him, the same beareth much fruite: for without me you can doe nothing.
If any abide not in me: he shal be cast forth as the branche, and shal wither, and they shal gather him vp, and cast him into the fire, and he burneth.
If you <na>[1]</na> abide in me, and my wordes abide in you: you shal aske what thing soeuer you wil, and it shal be done to you. ⊢

notes.text: If a Schismatike pray neuer so much, he is not heard, because he remayneth not in the body of Christ.

verses.text: In this my father is glorified: that you bring very much fruite, and become my Disciples.
As my father hath loued me, I also haue loued you. Abide in my loue.
If you keepe my precepts, you shal abide in my loue: as I also haue kept my fathers precepts, and doe abide in his loue.
These things I haue spoken to you, that my ioy may be in you, and your ioy may be filled.
<cr>[1]</cr> This is my precept, that you loue one an other, as I haue loued you.
<na>[1]</na> Greater loue then this no man hath, that a man yeld his life for his frendes.

notes.text: The Gospel upon S. Barnabee's day, and on the eves of some Apostles.

verses.text: You are my frendes, if you doe the things that I commaund you.
Now I cal you not seruants: for the seruant knoweth not what his lord doeth. But you I haue called frendes: because al things whatsoeuer I heard of my father, I haue notified vnto you.
You chose not me, but I chose you: and haue appointed you: that you goe, & bring fruite: and your fruite abide: that whatsoeuer you aske the father in my name, he may giue it you. ⊢
These things I commaund you, that you loue one an other.
<na>[1]</na> If the vvorld hate you: know ye that it hath hated me before you.

notes.text: The Gospel vpon SS. Simon and Iudes day.

verses.text: If you had been of the vvorld, the world would loue his owne. but because you are not of the world, but I haue chosen you out of the world, therfore the world hateth you.

Remembre my word that I said to you, <cr>[1]</cr> The seruant is not greater then his maister. If they haue persecuted me, you also wil they persecute. if they haue kept my word, <na>[2]</na> yours also wil they keepe.

notes.text: He foresheweth that many wil not obey the Churches wordes, & no maruel, because they contemned Christes owne precepts.

verses.text: But al these things they wil doe to you for my name sake: because they knovv not him that sent me.
If I had not come, and spoken to them, they should not haue sinne: but novv they haue no excuse of their sinne.
He that hateth me, hateth my Father also.
If I had not done among them vvorkes that no other man hath done, they should not haue sinne: but novv both they haue seen, and they doe hate both me and my Father.
But that the vvord may be fulfilled, vvhich is vvritten in their lavv: That they hated me gratis. ⊢ [1]
<cr>[1]</cr> But vvhen the Paraclete commeth vvhom I <na>[2]</na> vvil send you from the Father, the Spirit of truth, vvhich procedeth from the Father, he shal giue testimonie of me:

notes.text: The Gospel vpon Sunday after the Ascension, and in a Votiue of the B. Trinitie.

verses.text: and you shal giue testimonie, because you are vvith me from the beginning.

chapters.summary: He exhorteth them to abide in him (that is, his Church, being the true vine, and not the Synagogue of the Iewes any more) 9 and in his loue, louing one an other, and keeping his commaundements: 13 shewing how much he accounteth of them, by this that he dieth for them, 15 and reuealeth vnto them the secretes of heauen, 17 and appointeth their fruite to be perpetual: 18 confirming them also against the persecutions and hatred of the obstinate Iewes.

verses.text: apprehension, they will all forsake him.
<sc>THESE</sc> things haue I spoken to you, that you be not scandalized.
Out of the synagogs they vvil <na>[1]</na> cast you: but the houre commeth, that euery one vvhich killeth you, shal thinke that he doeth seruice to God.

notes.text: The Heretikes translate, Excommunicate you. See what corruption this is, and the reason thereof, Annot. c. 9, 22.

verses.text: and these things they vvil doe to you: because they haue not knovven the Father, nor me.
But these things I haue spoken to you: that vvhen the houre shal come, you may remember them, that I told you. ⊢
But I told you not these things from the beginning, because I vvas vvith you. And novv I goe to him that sent me, and none of you asketh me: VVhither goest thou?
<na>[1]</na> But because I haue spoken these things to you, sorovv hath filled your hart.

notes.text: The Gospel vpon the 4 Sunday after Easter.

verses.text: But I tel you the truth. it is expedient for you that I goe. For if I goe not, the Paraclete shal not come to you: but if I goe, I vvil send him to you.
And vvhen he is come, he shal argue the vvorld of sinne, and of iustice, and of iudgement.
of sinne: because they beleeue not in me.
but of iustice: because I goe to the Father: and novv you shal not see me.
and of iudgement: because the prince of this vvorld is now iudged.
Yet many things I haue to say to you: but you can not beare them novv.

But vvhen he, the Spirit of truth, commeth, <na>[1]</na> he shal teach you al truth. for he shal not speake of him self: but vvhat things soeuer he shal heare, he shal speake: and the things that are to come he shal shew you.

notes.text: If he shal teach al truth, & that for euer (as before c. 14, 16:) how is it possible, that the Church can erre, or hath erred at any time or in any point?

verses.text: He shal glorifie me: because he shal receiue of mine, and shal shevv to you. ⊢
Al things vvhatsoeuer the Father hath, be mine. Therfore I said, that he shal receiue of mine, and shal shew to you.
<na>[1]</na> A litle vvhile, and novv you shal not see me: and againe a litle vvhile, and you shal see me: because I goe to the Father.

notes.text: The Gospel vpon the 3 Sunday after Easter.

verses.text: Some therfore of his disciples said one to an other, VVhat is this that he saith to vs: A litle vvhile, and you shal not see me: and againe a litle vvhile, and you shal see me, and, because I goe to the Father?
They said therfore, VVhat is this that he saith, A litle vvhile? vve know not vvhat he speaketh.

And <sc>IESVS</sc> knew, that they vvould aske him: and he said to them, Of this you doe question among your selues, because I said to you, A litle vvhile, and you shal not see me: and againe a litle vvhile, and you shal see me.
<na>[1]</na> Amen, amen I say to you, that you shal vveepe, and lament, but the vvorld shal reioyce: and you shal be made sorovvful, but your sorow shal be turned into ioy.

notes.text: The Gospel for some Martyrs between Easter. & Whitsunday.

verses.text: A vvoman vvhen she trauaileth, hath sorovv, because her houre is come: but vvhen she hath brought forth the childe, novv she remembreth not the anguish for ioy, that a man is borne into the vvorld.
And you therfore, novv in deede you haue sorow, but I vvil see you againe, and your hart shal reioyce: and your ioy no man shal take from you. ⊢
<na>[1]</na> And in that day me you shal not aske any thing. Amen, amen I say to you, if you aske the Father any thing <na>[2]</na> in my name, he vvil giue it you.

notes.text: The Gospel vpon the 5 Sunday after Easter.
Vpon this the Church concludeth al her praiers, Per Christum Dominum nostrū, euen those also that be made to Saincts.

verses.text: Vntil novv you haue not asked any thing in my name. Aske and you shal receiue: that your ioy may be ful.
These things in prouerbes I haue spoken to you. The houre commeth vvhen in prouerbes I vvil no more speake to you, but plainely of the Father I vvil shew you.
In that day you shal aske in my name: and I say not to you, that I vvil aske the Father for you.
For the Father him self loueth you, because you haue loued me, and haue beleeued that I came forth from God.
I came forth from the Father, and came into the vvorld: againe I leaue the vvorld, and I goe to the Father.
His disciples say to him, Behold novv thou speakest plainely, and saiest no prouerbe.
novv vve know that thou knovvest al things, and thou needest not that any man aske thee. in this vve beleeue that thou camest forth from God. ⊢
<sc>IESVS</sc> ansvvered them, Novv do you beleeue?
<cr>[1]</cr> Behold the houre commeth, and it is novv come, that you shal be scattered euery man into his ovvne, and me you shal leaue alone: and I am not alone, because the Father is vvith me.
These things I haue spoken to you, that in me you may haue peace. In the vvorld you shal haue distresse: but haue confidence, I haue ouercome the vvorld.

chapters.summary: The cause why he foretelleth them their persecution by the Iewes, is, that they be not afterward scandalized thereat. 6 Though they thinke this heauie newes, it is for their vantage that he departeth, because of the great benefites that they shal receiue by the comming then of the Holy Ghost, who shal also be his witnes against his enemies. 16 Although in this world they shal so be persecuted, yet to his heauenly Father they and their praiers made in his name, shal be most acceptable. and at length the childe (that is, Christ in al his members) being borne, their ioy shal be such as no persecutor can take from them. 31 Howbeit at this instant of his apprehension, they wil al forsake him.

verses.text: <sc>THESE</sc> <na>[1]</na> things spake <sc>IESVS</sc>: and lifting vp his eies into heauen, he said, Father, the houre is come, <na>[2]</na> glorifie thy sonne, that thy sonne may glorifie thee.

notes.text: The Gospel vpon Ascension eue.

The Father glorifieth the Sonne by raising him from death, exalting him vp to his right hand, making al creatures to bow downe at his Name, and geuing him al power and iudgement. The Sonne againe glorifieth the Father, by making his honour, which onely in a maner was in Iewrie before, now knowen to al Nations.

verses.text: As thou hast giuen him povver ouer al flesh that al vvhich thou hast giuen him, to them he may giue life euerlasting.
And this is life euerlasting that they know thee, the only true God, and vvhom thou hast sent <sc>IESVS CHRIST</sc>.
I haue glorified thee vpon the earth: I haue consummated the worke vvhich thou gauest me to doe:
and novv glorifie thou me O Father with thy self, with the glorie vvhich I had before the world was, with thee.
I haue manifested thy name to the men whom thou gauest me out of the vvorld. Thine they were, and to me thou gauest them: and they haue kept thy vvord.
Now they haue knovven that al things which thou gauest me, are from thee:
because the wordes which thou gauest me, I haue giuen them: and they haue receiued, and knowen in very deede that I came forth from thee, and haue beleeued that thou didst send me.
For them doe I pray: Not for the world doe I pray, but for them vvhom thou hast giuen me:
because they be thine: and al my things be thine, and thine be mine: and I am glorified in them. And novv I am not in the world, and these are in the vvorld, and I come to thee. ⊢
<na>[1]</na> Holy father, <na>[2]</na> keepe them in thy name, whom thou hast giuen me: that they may be one, as also vve.

notes.text: The Gospel in a Votiue Masse against Schisme.
His petition is specially to keepe the Apostles and his Church in vnitie and from Schismes.

verses.text: When I was with them, I kept them in thy name. Those <cr>[1]</cr> vvhom thou gauest me, haue I kept: and none of them perished, but the sonne of perdition, that the <cr>[2]</cr> scripture may be fulfilled.
And now I come to thee: and these things I speake in the world, that they may haue my ioy filled in them selues.
I haue giuen them thy vvord, and the vvorld hath hated them, because they are not of the vvorld: as I also am not of the world.
I pray not that thou take them avvay out of the vvorld, but that thou preserue them from euil.
Of the vvorld they are not: as I also am not of the vvorld.
Sanctifie them in truth. Thy vvord is truth.
As thou didst send me into the vvorld, I also haue sent them into the vvorld.
And for thē I doe <na>[1]</na> sanctifie my self: that they also may be sanctified in truth.

notes.text: To sanctifie him self, is to sacrifice him self, by dedicating his holy body and bloud to his Father, both vpon the Crosse, and in the holy Sacrament.

verses.text: And not for them only doe I pray, but for them also that by their vvord shal beleeue in me:
that they al may be one, as thou (Father) in me, and I in thee, that they also in vs may be one: that the vvorld may beleeue that thou hast sent me.
And the glorie that thou hast giuen me, haue I giuen to them: that they may be one, as vve also are one.
I in them, and thou in me: that they may be consummate in one: ⊢ and the vvorld may knovv that thou hast sent me, and hast loued them, as me also thou hast loued.

Father, vvhom thou hast giuen me, I vvil, that vvhere I am, they also may be vvith me: that they maye see my glorie vvhich thou hast giuen me, because thou hast loued me before the creation of the vvorld.
Iust Father, the vvorld hath not knovven thee. but I haue knovven thee: and these haue knovven, that thou didst send me.
And I haue notified thy name to them, and vvil notifie it: that the loue vvhervvith thou hast loued me may be in them, and I in them.

chapters.summary: After his Sermon of farewel, he prayeth to his Father, that seing he hath now finished his worke, he wil giue him his appointed glorie, for the conuersion of al nations, 6 and preserue his Apostles, and his Church after them in vnitie and veritie (that is, from Schisme and Heresie:) 24 finally also glorifie them with him in heauen.

verses.text: <sc>WHEN <cr>[1]</cr><na>[2]</na> IESVS</sc> had said these things, he went forth vvith his disciples beyond the Torrent-Cedron, vvhere vvas a garden, into the vvhich he entred and his Disciples.

notes.text: THURSDAY night. The PASSION according to S. John in these two Chapters, is the Gospel at Mass upon Good Friday. So the PASSION is read in Holy Week four times, according to the four Evangelists, as S. Augustine appointed also in his Church at Hippo. Ser. 144. de tempore.

verses.text: And Iudas also, that betraied him, knevv the place: because <sc>IESVS</sc> had often resorted thither together vvith his Disciples.
<cr>[1]</cr> Iudas therfore hauing receiued the band of men, and of the cheefe Priests and the Pharisees, ministers, commeth thither vvith lanternes and torches and vveapons.
<sc>IESVS</sc> therfore knovving al things that should come vpon him, vvent forth, and said to them, VVhom seeke ye?
they ansvvered him, <sc>IESVS</sc> of Nazareth. <sc>IESVS</sc> saith to them, I am he. And Iudas also that betraied him, stoode vvith them.
As sone therfore as he said to them, I am he: they vvent backvvard, and fel to the ground.
Againe therfore he asked them, VVhom seeke ye? And they said, <sc>IESVS</sc> of Nazareth.
<sc>IESVS</sc> answered, I haue told you, that I am he. if therfore you seeke me, let these goe their vvaies.
That the word might be fulfilled vvhich he said, <cr>[1]</cr> That of them vvhom thou hast giuen me, I haue not lost any.
Simon Peter therfore hauing a svvord, drevve it out: and smote the seruant of the high priest: & cut of his right eare. And the name of the seruant vvas Malchus.
<sc>IESVS</sc> therfore said to Peter, Put vp thy sword into the scabbard. The chalice vvhich my father hath giuen me, shal not I drinke it?
The band therfore and the Tribune & the ministers of the Ievves apprehended <sc>IESVS</sc>, and bound him:
and they brought him to Annas first, for he vvas father in lavv to Caiphas, vvho vvas the high priest of that yere.
And <cr>[1]</cr> Caiphas vvas he that had giuen the counsel to the Iewes, That it is expedient that one man die for the people.
<cr>[1]</cr> And Simon Peter folovved <sc>IESVS</sc>, and an other disciple. And that Disciple vvas knovven to the high priest, and vvent in with <sc>IESVS</sc> into the court of the high priest.
but Peter stoode at the doore without. The other disciple therfore that vvas knovven to the high Priest, vvent forth, and spake to the portresse, and brought in Peter.
The vvench therfore that vvas portresse, saith to Peter, Art not thou also of this mans disciples? He saith to her, <na>[1]</na> I am not.

notes.text: It is al one for a man to deny Christ, and, that he is a disciple of Christ, or a Catholike, or a Christian man, when he is demaunded. Aug. tract. 113 in Io. for so Peter here denieth Christ, in denying him self to be his Disciple.

verses.text: And the seruants and ministers stoode at a fire of coles, because it was cold, and vvarmed them selues. And vvith them vvas Peter also standing, and vvarming him self.
The high priest therfore asked <sc>IESVS</sc> of his disciples, and of his doctrine.

<sc>IESVS</sc> answered him, I haue openly spoken to the vvorld: I haue alvvaies taught in the synagogue, and in the temple vvhither al the Ievves resort together: and in secrete I haue spoken nothing.
VVhy askest thou me? aske them that haue heard vvhat I haue spoken vnto them: behold they knovv vvhat things I haue said.
VVhen he had said these things, one of the ministers standing by, gaue <sc>IESVS</sc> a blovv, saying, Ansvverest thou the high priest so?
<sc>IESVS</sc> ansvvered him, If I haue spoken il, giue testimonie of euil: but if vvel, vvhy strikest thou me?
And Annas sent him bound to Caiphas the high priest.
And Simon Peter vvas standing, and vvarming him self. They said therfore to him, Art not thou also of his disciples? He denied and said: I am not.
One of the seruants of the high priest saith to him, his cosin whose eare Peter did cut of, Did not I see thee in the garden vvith him?
Againe therfore Peter denied: and forth with the cocke crevve.

<cr>[1]</cr><na>[2]</na> They therfore bring <sc>IESVS</sc> from Caiphas into the Palace. And it vvas morning: and they vvent not in into the Palace, that they might not be contaminated, but that they might eate the Pasche.

notes.text: GOOD FRIDAY.

verses.text: Pilate therfore vvent forth to them vvithout, and said, VVhat accusation bring you against this man?
They ansvvered and said to him, If he vvere not a malefactour, vve vvould not haue deliuered him vp to thee.
Pilate therfore said to them, Take him you, and according to your lavv iudge him. The Ievves therfore said to him, It is not lavvful for vs to kil any man.
<cr>[1]</cr> That the vvord of <sc>IESVS</sc> might be fulfilled vvhich he said, signifying what death he should die.
<cr>[1]</cr> Pilate therfore vvent into the Palace againe, and called <sc>IESVS</sc>, and said to him, Art thou the king of the Ievves?
<sc>IESVS</sc> ansvvered, Saiest thou this of thy self, or haue others told it thee of me?
Pilate answered, VVhy, am I a Iewe? <na>[1]</na> Thy nation, and the cheefe priests haue deliuered thee vp to me: vvhat hast thou done?

notes.text: It pleased God, that Christ who was to dy both for the Iewes & the Gētiles, should be betraied of the one, and put to death by the other.

verses.text: <sc>IESVS</sc> ansvvered, My kingdom is not of this vvorld. if my kingdom vvere of this vvorld, my ministers verily vvould striue that I should not be deliuered to the Ievves. but novv my kingdom is not from hence.

Pilate therfore said to him, Art thou a king then? <sc>IESVS</sc> answered, Thou saiest, that I am a king. For this was I borne, and for this came I into the world: that I should giue testimonie to the truth. Euery one that is of the truth, heareth my voice.
Pilate saith to him, VVhat is truth? And vvhen he had said this, he vvent forth againe to the Ievves, and saith to them, I finde no cause in him.
<cr>[1]</cr> But you haue a custome that I should release one to you in the Pasche: vvil you therfore that I release vnto you the king of the Ievves?
They al therfore cried againe, saying, Not him but Barabbas. And Barabbas vvas a theefe.

chapters.summary: Being gone to the place that Iudas the Traitor did know, 4 he offereth him self to the hand of his enemies, showeth his Diuine might in ouerthrowing them al with a word, and in sauing his Apostles from them also with a word: 10 rebuketh Peter that would defend him from them: 12 and so being apprehended, is brought bound to Annas and Caiphas, where he is striken by a seruant, and thrise denied of Peter. 28 Againe in the morning he is by them brought to Pilate. 29 Who demaunding their accusation, whereas they would oppresse him with their authoritie, 33 and examining the point of his kingdom, pronounceth him innocent: yet they crie rather to haue a theeues life saued.

verses.text: <sc>THEN</sc> therfore Pilate tooke <sc>IESVS</sc>, and scourged him. <cr>[1]</cr>
And the souldiars platting a crowne of thornes, put it vpon his head: and they put about him a purple garment.
And they came to him, and said, Haile king of the Ievves, and they gaue him blovves.
Pilate vvent forth againe, and saith to them, Behold I bring him forth vnto you, that you may know that I finde no cause in him.
<sc>IESVS</sc> therfore vvent forth carying the crovvne of thornes, and the purple vestiment. And he saith to them, Loe the man.
When the cheefe priests therfore and the ministers had seen him, they cried, saying, Crucifie, crucifie him. Pilate saith to them, Take him you, and crucifie him. for I finde no cause in him.
The Ievves ansvvered him, VVe haue a Law: and according to the Law he ought to die, because he hath made him self the sonne of God.
When Pilate therfore had heard this saying, he feared more.
And he entred into the Palace againe: and he saith to <sc>IESVS</sc>, VVhence art thou? But <sc>IESVS</sc> gaue him no ansvver.
Pilate therfore saith to him, Speakest thou not to me? knovvest thou not that I haue povver to crucifie thee, and I haue povver to release thee?
<sc>IESVS</sc> ansvvered, Thou shouldest not haue any povver against me, vnles it vvere giuen thee from aboue. Therfore he that hath betraied me to thee, hath the greater sinne.
From thence forth Pilate sought to release him. But the Iewes cried, saying, If thou release this man, thou art not Cæsars frend. euery one that maketh him self a king, speaketh against Cæsar.
But Pilate vvhen he had heard these vvordes, brought forth <sc>IESVS</sc>: and he sate in the iudgement seate, in the place that is called Lithóstrotos, and in Hebrew Gábbatha.
And it vvas the Parasceue of Pasche, about the <na>[1]</na> sixt houre, and he saith to the Ievves, Loe your king.

notes.text: He meaneth midday, counting from sunne rising. for so doth the Scripture count the houres of the day. Mat. 20. Mar. 15. Luc, 23. Io. 4. Act. 3 & 10.

verses.text: But they cried, Avvay, avvay vvith him, crucifie him. Pilate saith to them, Shal I crucifie your king? The cheefe priests answered, VVe haue no king, but Cæsar.
Then therfore he deliuered him vnto them for to be crucified. And they tooke <sc>IESVS</sc>, and led him forth.
<cr>[1]</cr> And bearing his ovvne crosse he went forth into that vvhich is called the place of Caluarie, in Hebrew Gólgotha.
vvhere they crucified him, and vvith him two others, on the one side and on the other, and in the middes <sc>IESVS</sc>.
And Pilate wrote a title also: and he put it vpon the crosse. And it vvas written, <sc>IESVS OF NAZARETH THE KING OF THE IEWES</sc>.
This title therfore many of the Ievves did reade: because the place vvhere <sc>IESVS</sc> vvas crucified, vvas nigh to the citie: and it was vvritten in <na>[1]</na> Hebrevv, in Greeke, and in Latin.

notes.text: These three tongues being for other causes most famous before in al the world, are now also dedicated to God in the triumphans title of the Crosse of Christ, and in them the holy Scriptures are more conueniently Written, taught, & preserued.

verses.text: The cheefe priests therfore of the Ievves said to Pilate, VVrite not, The king of the Iewes: but that he said, I am king of the Iewes.
Pilate ansvvered, That vvhich I haue written, I haue vvritten.

The <cr>[1]</cr> souldiars therfore vvhen they had crucified him, tooke his garments (and they made foure partes, to euery souldiar a part) & his coate. And his <na>[2]</na> coate vvas vvithout seame, wrought from the toppe through out.

notes.text: Mt. 27. 35. Mr. 15, 24. Luc. 23, 34. · This coate without seame is a figure of the vnitie of the Church. Cypr. de vnit. Ec. And Euthymius and other write that our Lady made it.

verses.text: They said therfore one to an other, Let vs not cut it, but let vs cast lottes for it vvhose it shal be. That the scripture might be fulfilled saying, They haue parted my garments among them: and vpon my vesture they haue cast lottes. [1] And the souldiars did these things.
<na>[1]</na> And there stoode beside the crosse of <sc>IESVS</sc>, <na>[2]</na> his mother, and his mothers sister, Marie of Cléphas, and Marie Magdalene.

notes.text: The Gospel in a votiue Masse of our B. Lady betweene Easter & Whitsuntide.
The great loue faith, courage, compassion, and sorowes, that our Lady had: who forsooke not the Crosse and her sonne, when so many were fled from him, and his cheefe Apostles denied him.

verses.text: VVhen <sc>IESVS</sc> therfore had seen his mother and the disciple standing vvhom he loued, he saith to his mother: VVoman, behold thy sonne.
After that, he saith to the disciple, Behold thy mother. And from that houre the disciple tooke her to his ovvne.
xrefs: The Gospel in a votiue Masse of the Passion.

verses.text: <cr>[1]</cr> Aftervvard <sc>IESVS</sc> knovving that al things vvere novv consummate, that the <na>[2]</na> scripture might be fulfilled, he saith, I thirst.

notes.text: b The Gospel in a votive Mass of the Passion.

verses.text: A vessel therfore stoode there ful of vinegre. And they putting a spongeful of vinegre about hyssope, offered it to his mouth.
<sc>IESVS</sc> therfore vvhen he had taken the vinegre, said, It is consummate. And bovving his head, he gaue vp the ghost.

The Ievves therfore (because it vvas the Parasceue) that the bodies might not remaine vpon the crosse on the Sabboth (for that vvas a greate Sabboth day) they desired Pilate that their legges might be broken, and they might be taken avvay.
The souldiars therfore came: and of the first in deede they brake the legges, and of the other that vvas crucified vvith him.
But after they vvere come to <sc>IESVS</sc>, vvhen they savv that he vvas dead, they did not breake his legges,
but one of the souldiars vvith a speare opened his side, and incontinent there came forth bloud and vvater.
And he that saw it, hath giuen testimonie: and his testimonie is true. And he knovveth that he saith true, that you also may beleeue.
For these things vvere done that the scripture might be fulfilled, You shal not breake a bone of him. [1]
And againe an other scripture saith, They shal looke on him whom they pearsed. [1]

And after these things <cr>[1]</cr> Ioseph of Arimathaea (because he vvas a disciple of <sc>IESVS</sc>, but secrete for feare of the Iewes) desired Pilate that he might take avvay the body of <sc>IESVS</sc>. And Pilate permitted. He came therfore, and tooke away the body of <sc>IESVS</sc>.
<cr>[1]</cr> Nicodemus also came, he that at the first came to <sc>IESVS</sc> by the night, bringing a mixture of myrrhe and aloés, about an hundred poundes.
They tooke therfore the body of <sc>IESVS</sc>, and bound it in linnen clothes with the spices, as the maner is vvith the Ievves to burie.
And there vvas in the place vvhere he vvas crucified, a garden: and in the garden a nevv monument, vvherein no man yet had been laide.
There therfore because of the Parasceue of the Ievves, they laid <sc>IESVS</sc>, because the monument vvas hard by.

chapters.summary: The Iewes are not satisfied with his scourging and irrision. 8 Pilate hearing them say that he made him self the Sonne of God, is more afraid. 12 Yet, they vrging him with his loialty toward Cæsar, and professing that them selues wil no king but Cæsar, he yeldeth vnto them. 17 And so Christ carying his owne Crosse, is crucified betwene two theeues, 19 Pilate writing notoriously the onely cause of his death to be, for that he is their king or Christ. 23 His garments be so vsed, euen as the Scriptures foretold. 25 He hath special care of his mother to the end. 28 He signifieth al that was written of his Passion, to be fulfilled, and so yeldeth vp his ghost. 31 Then by the Iewes meanes also other Scriptures about his legges and side, are fulfilled. 38 And finally, he is honorably buried.

verses.text: <sc>AND</sc> <cr>[1]</cr><na>[2]</na> the <na>[3]</na> first of the Sabboth, Marie Magdalene commeth early, when it was yet darke, vnto the monument: and she saw the stone taken away from the monument.

notes.text: The Gospel vpon Saturday in Easter weeke.

That is, the first day of the weeke, as some interprete it, taking Sabboth (as sometime it is) for a weeke. This is our Sunday, called Dies Dominica, because of our Lords resurrection. See the marg. annot. Luc. 24, 1.

verses.text: She ranne therfore and commeth to Simon Peter, and to the other disciple whom <sc>IESVS</sc> loued, and saith to them, They haue taken our Lord out of the monument, and we know not where they haue laid him.
Peter therfore went forth and that other disciple, and they came to the monument.
And both ranne together, and that other disciple did out-runne Peter, and came first to the monument. <cr>[1]</cr>
And when he had stouped downe, he saw the linnen clothes lying: but yet he went not in.
Simon Peter therfore commeth, folowing him, and went in to the monument, and saw the linnen clothes lying,
and the napkin that had been vpon his head, not lying with the linnen clothes, but apart, wrapped vp into one place.
Then therfore went in that other disciple also which came first to the monument: and he saw, and beleeued.
For as yet they knew not the scripture, that he should rise againe from the dead. ⊢
The disciples therfore departed againe to them selues.
b <cr>[1]</cr> But <na>[2]</na> Marie stoode at the <na>[3]</na> monument without, weeping. Therfore as she was weeping, she stouped downe, & looked into the monument:

notes.text: The Gospel vpon Thursday in Easter weeke.

The Sepulchres of Martyrs (saith S. Hierom ep. 17) we do honour euery where, & putting their holy ashes to our eies, if we may, we touch it also with our mouth: and be there some that thinke the monument wherein our Lord was laid, is to be neglected: where the Diuel and his Angels, as often as they are cast out of the possessed before the said monument, tremble and roare as if they stoode before the iudgement seate of Christ?

verses.text: and she saw two Angels in white, sitting, one at the head, and one at the feete, where the body of <sc>IESVS</sc> had been laid.
They say to her, Woman, why weepest thou? She saith to them, Because they haue taken away my Lord, and I know not where they haue put him.
When she had said thus, she turned backward, and saw <sc>IESVS</sc> standing: and she knew not that it is <sc>IESVS</sc>.

<sc>IESVS</sc> saith to her, Woman, why weepest thou? whom seekest thou? She thinking that it was the gardiner, saith to him, Sir, if thou hast caried him away, tel me where thou hast laid him: & I wil take him away.
<sc>IESVS</sc> saith to her, Marie. She turning saith to him, Rabbóni (which is to say, Maister.)
<sc>IESVS</sc> saith to her, Do not touche me, for I am not yet ascended to my Father: but goe to my brethren, and say to them, I ascend to my Father and your Father, my God and your God.
Marie Magdalene commeth and telleth the disciples, That I haue seen our Lord, and thus he said vnto me.

<cr>[1]</cr> Therfore vvhen it vvas <na>[2]</na> late that day, the first of the Sabboths, and the doores vvere shut, where the disciples vvere gathered together for feare of the Iewes, <sc>IESVS</sc> came and stoode in the middes, and saith to them, Peace be to you.

notes.text: The Gospel vpon Dominica in albis or Low Sunday.

verses.text: And vvhen he had said this, he shewed them his handes and side. The disciples therfore vvere glad vvhen they savv our Lord.
He said therfore to them againe, <na>[1]</na> Peace be to you. As my Father hath sent me, I also doe send you.

notes.text: Though he gaue them his peace hard before, yet now entering to a new diuine action, to prepare their hartes to grace and attention, he blesseth them againe.

verses.text: When he had said this, he breathed vpon them: and he saith to them, Receiue ye the Holy Ghost:
<sc>VVHOSE SINNES YOV SHAL FORGIVE, THEY ARE FORGIVEN THEM: AND WHOSE YOV SHAL RETEINE, THEY ARE RETEINED</sc>.
<na>[1]</na> But Thomas one of the Tvvelue, vvho is called Didymus, vvas not vvith them when <sc>IESVS</sc> came.

notes.text: The Gospel vpon S. Thomas the Apostles day, Decemb. 21.

verses.text: The other disciples therfore said to him, VVe haue seen our Lord. But he said to them, Vnles I see in his handes the print of the nailes, and put my finger into the place of the nailes, and put my hand into his side: I vvil not beleeue.

<na>[1]</na> And after eight daies, againe his disciples vvere vvithin: and Thomas vvith them. <sc>IESVS</sc> commeth <na>[2]</na> the doores being shut, and stoode in the middes, and said, Peace be to you.

notes.text: LOW SVNDAY.
See the annotation on the 19 verse of this Chapter.

verses.text: Then he saith to Thomas, Put in thy finger hither, and see my handes, and bring hither thy hand, and put it into my side: & be not incredulous but faithful.
Thomas ansvvered, & said to him, My Lord, & my God.
<sc>IESVS</sc> saith to him, Because thou hast seen me, Thomas, thou hast beleeued: <na>[1]</na> blessed are they that haue not seen & haue beleeued.

notes.text: They are more happy that beleeue without sensible argument or sight, then such as be induced by sense or reason to beleeue.

verses.text: <cr>[1]</cr> Many other signes also did <sc>IESVS</sc> in the sight of his disciples, vvhich are not written in this booke.
And these are vvritten, that you may beleeue that <sc>IESVS</sc> is <sc>CHRIST</sc> the sonne of God: and that beleeuing, you may haue life in his name.

chapters.summary: Vpon Easter day his body is missed in the Sepulcher, first by M. Magdalene, 3 secondly by Peter also and Iohn, the winding clothes yet remayning. 11 Then to M. Magdalene, after she had seen two Angels, IESVS also him self appeareth. 18 She hauing told to the Disciples, he appeareth to them also the same day, and sendeth them as him self was sent, giuing them the Holy Ghost to remitte and to reteine sinnes. 26 Againe vpon low Sunday he appeareth to them, letting Thomas see, that he might beleeue, and commending such as not seeing yet do beleeue. 30 The effect of this booke.

verses.text: <sc>AFTER <na>[1]</na> IESVS</sc> manifested him self againe at the sea of Tibérias. And he manifested thus:

notes.text: The Gospel on wenseday in Easter weeke.

verses.text: There vvere together Simon Peter and Thomas vvho is called Didymus, and Nathanael vvhich vvas of Cana in Galilee, and the sonnes of Zebedee, and tvvo others of his disciples.
Simon Peter saith to them, I goe to fish. They say to him, VVe also come vvith thee. And they vvent forth and got vp into the boate: and that night they tooke nothing.
But when morning vvas novv come, <sc>IESVS</sc> stoode on the shore: yet the disciples knevv not that it was <sc>IESVS</sc>.
<sc>IESVS</sc> therfore saith to them, Children, haue you any meate? They ansvvered him, No.
He saith to them, Cast the nette on the right side of the boate: and you shal finde. They therfore did cast it: and novv they vvere not able to dravv it for the multitude of fishes.

That disciple therfore vvhom <sc>IESVS</sc> loued, saith to Peter, It is our Lord. <na>[1]</na> Simon Peter when he had heard that it is our Lord: girded his coate vnto him (for he vvas naked) and cast him self into the sea.

notes.text: See in S. Augustine tract. 122 in Io. the great mysterie hereof concerning the CHVRCH, and in S. Gregorie hom. 24 in Euang. and S. Bernard li. 2 c. 8 de consid. Peters PRIMACIE here mistically signified.

verses.text: But the other disciples came in the boate (for they vvere not farre from the land, but as it vvere tvvo hundred cubits) dravving the nette of fishes.
Therefore after they came dovvne to land, they savv hote coles lying, and fish laid thereon, and bread.
<sc>IESVS</sc> saith to them, Bring hither of the fishes that you tooke novv.
Simon Peter vvent vp, and drevv the nette to the land, ful of great fishes, an hundred fiftie three. And although they vvere so many, the nette vvas not broken.
<sc>IESVS</sc> saith to them, Come, dine. And none of them that sate at meate, <na>[1]</na> durst aske him, Who art thou? knovving that it is our Lord.

notes.text: the disciples,

verses.text: And <sc>IESVS</sc> commeth and taketh the bread and giueth them, and the fish in like maner.
This novv the <na>[1]</na> third time <sc>IESVS</sc> vvas manifested to his disciples, after he vvas risen from the dead.

notes.text: Not the third apparition, but the third day of his apparitions. for he appeared in the very day of his Resurrection often, againe vpon Low Sunday, then this third time, And S. Marke saying, last he appeared, c. 16, 14: meaneth his last apparition the first day.

verses.text: <na>[1]</na> Therfore vvhen they had dined, <sc>IESVS</sc> saith to Simon Peter, Simon of Iohn, louest thou me more then these? He saith to him, Yea Lord: thou knovvest that I loue thee. he saith to him, <sc>FEEDE MY LAMBES</sc>.

notes.text: The Gospel on the eue of SS. Peter and Paul.

verses.text: He saith to him againe, Simon of Iohn, louest thou me? he saith to him, Yea Lord, thou knovvest that I loue thee. He saith to him, <na>[1]</na> <sc>FEEDE MY LAMBES</sc>.

notes.text: c ποίμαινε feed & rule.

verses.text: He saith to him the third time, Simon of Iohn, louest thou me? Peter vvas stroken sad, because he said vnto him the third time, Louest thou me? And he said to him, Lord, thou knowest al things: thou knovvest that I loue thee. He saith to him, <sc>FEEDE MY SHEEPE</sc>.

Amen, amen I say to thee, vvhen thou wast yonger, thou didst girde thy self, and didst vvalke vvhere thou vvouldest. but vvhen thou shalt be old, thou shalt stretch forth thy handes, and an other shal girde thee, and leade thee whither thou vvilt not.
And this he said, signifying by vvhat death he should glorifie God. <na>[1]</na> And vvhen he had said this, he saith to him, Folovv me.

notes.text: The Gospel vpon S. Iohn the Euangelists day in Christmas Decembris 27.

verses.text: Peter turning, savv that disciple whom <sc>IESVS</sc> loued, folovving, <cr>[1]</cr> vvho also leaned at the supper vpon his breast, and said, Lord vvho is he that shal betray thee?
Him therfore vvhen Peter had seen, he saith to <sc>IESVS</sc>, Lord, and this man vvhat?
<sc>IESVS</sc> saith to him, <na>[1]</na> So I vvil haue him to remaine til I come, vvhat to thee? folovv thou me.

notes.text: c So readeth S. Ambrose in Ps. 45. & ser. 20 in Ps. 118. S. Aug. tract. 124 in Io. & most ancient copies and service books extant in Latin. Others read, If I will: others, If so I will, &c.

xrefs: So readeth S. Ambrose in Ps. 45. & ser. 20 in Ps. 118. S. Aug. tract. 124 in Io. & most ancient copies and seruice bookes extant in Latine, other reade, If I wil: other, If so I wil &c.

verses.text: This saying therfore went abrode among the brethren, that that disciple dieth not. And <sc>IESVS</sc> did not say to him, he dieth not: but, So I vvil haue him to remaine til I come, what to thee?
This is that disciple vvhich giueth testimonie of these things, and hath vvritten these things: and vve knovv that his testimonie is true.

But there are <cr>[1]</cr> many <cr>[2]</cr> other things also vvhich <sc>IESVS</sc> did: vvhich if they vvere vvritten in particular, neither the world it self I thinke vvere able to conteine those bookes that should be vvritten.

notes.text: Beza in hunc locum.

How few things are written of Christs actes & doctrine in comparison of that which he did and spake? and yet the Heretikes wil needes haue al in Scripture, trusting not the Apostles owne preaching, or report of any thing that our Maister did or said, if it be not written.

chapters.summary: Appearing againe in Galilee, where Peter was fishing with his fellowes: and causing them after they had al night taken none, to catch a great multitude, which Peter draweth to land, where he also dineth them: 15 He (expressing what this fishing signified) maketh Peter his Vicar, committing vnto him the feeding of his lambes and sheepe: 18 and reuealeth vnto him, that he also shal be crucified, to the glorie of God, 20 admonishing him to minde that, rather then to be curious about Iohns death.
